#2254. Celtic fans disgracefully boo during minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday: Referee ends tribute after just 13 SECONDS - even after warning from the PA announcer

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:28 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:51 EST, 9 November 2026

Celtic were forced to curtail plans to commemorate Remembrance Day after a section of their supporters booed during the planned minute's silence on Remembrance Sunday.

The Bhoys hosted Kilmarnock in the Scottish Premiership on Sunday - with Liam Scales' goal proving the difference in a 1-0 win.

However, ahead of kick-off at Parkhead, the annual tribute to the armed forces and their families was overshadowed by some fans' loud jeers.

As the players from both teams gathered around the centre-circle, an announcement on the public address system said: 'We will have a minute's silence today on Remembrance Sunday to remember all victims of all conflicts. We remember, in particular, the men who served Celtic football club and lost their lives at wartime.'

The audible disdain resulted in referee John Beaton being forced to cut the silence after just 13 seconds.

The noise was so palpable that the Celtic TV broadcast turned down the volume to try and minimise its impact too.

The minute's silence ahead of Celtic versus Kilmarnock was cut short due to some fans booing

Celtic TV turned down the volume to try and minimise the jeers during the curtailed silence

Referee John Beaton (right) cut the minute's silence after 13 seconds as a result of the booing

Furthermore, the lower tier of the standing section was empty until the Green Brigade and other fans started to file in from the concourse when referee Beaton’s whistle signalled the end of the tribute.

Football clubs across the United Kingdom observe a minute's silence with their nearest home fixture around Remembrance Sunday and Armistice Day - with the latter on November 11.

Many teams also wear poppies, something Kilmarnock wore on their strip, but Celtic didn't.

Some Celtic supporters refuse to partake in the tradition or actively take a stance against it, often citing the club’s Irish roots and linking it to the British Army‘s role in The Troubles.

Last season, in a quirk, Celtic hosted Kilmarnock on Remembrance Sunday too - with that minute's silence also cut short due to jeering. That time referee Don Robertson cut it short at 15 seconds.

As well as the booing in that match last term, some fans turned their back on the minute's silence and also made gestures.

Sunday's 1-0 win over Kilmarnock sees Celtic regain their four-point lead at the top of the Scottish Premiership.

It was under-pressure Martin O'Neill's side's first league win in their last three games.

Scales scored the only goal of the game on 26 minutes when he hooked a Camilo Duran cross into the top corner.

Celtic fans show their displeasure during the minute's silence for Remembrance Day in 2025

Celtic - and Kasper Hogh in particular - otherwise had a frustrating day in front of goal, with Benjamin Nygren missing a second-half penalty.

Hogh had an early goal disallowed as his barren run without a goal hit the 16-game mark since he netted a hat-trick at Kilmarnock on his second appearance.

Celtic have 31 points from their opening 13 matches - four more than bitter rivals Rangers who sit second but have a game in hand.

Kilmarnock remain rooted to the bottom of the table with nine points from 13 games - two adrift of 11th-place Aberdeen who have played a match fewer.

#2253. La lettera di addio di Michael Carrick al Manchester United

Michael Carrick è stato esonerato. L'incubo dei tifosi del Manchester United non sembra conoscere una fine e, anzi, si fa sempre più realistico dal momento che dopo metà girone d'andata i Red Devils si ritrovano in piena zona retrocessione. Il tecnico, ed ex giocatore, è stato sollevato dal suo incarico nella giornata di giovedì e il giorno dopo è stato annunciato già il suo sostituto, Mauricio Pochettino.

Intanto Michael Carrick ha salutato il Manchester United e i suoi tifosi con una lunga lettera d'addio: "Cari tifosi dello United, ho avuto l'immenso onore di guidare il Manchester United, il club che amo. Sono incredibilmente grato di aver vissuto e sentito tutto ciò. Lo United è diverso da qualsiasi altro posto e per starci devi capire cosa significa. Devi spingere per essere il migliore, ma ci sono cultura, valori e comportamenti che devi vivere e rispettare, costruiti nel corso del tempo. Questo club è unico e ha una storia che non si deve ignorare. Voglio ringraziare voi tifosi, siete rari e speciali. Abbiamo vissuto momenti fantastici ed istanti che ricorderemo".

Continua Carrick: "So che, ultimamente, non abbiamo ottenuto risultati, ma mi avete mostrato amore e sostegno in un momento in cui la cosa più facile da fare sarebbe stata voltare le spalle. Non l'avete fatto è ciò vale più di una vittoria. Ecco perché mi sono innamorato di questo club tanti anni fa. Ringrazio il mio staff tecnico. Avete dato tutto ogni singolo giorno e non avrei potuto chiedere di più. Vi voglio ringraziare per la lealtà, il duro lavoro ed il sostegno durante questo periodo".

Infine Carrick chiude: "Voglio ringraziare i giocatori per gli sforzi ed i momenti che abbiamo condiviso. Vi auguro il meglio per il futuro. Io voglio solo il successo per il Manchester United. Questo club è stato una parte così grande ed importante della mia vita e ciò non cambierà mai. Sarò sempre orgoglioso di aver dato il mio contributo e vorrò sempre il meglio per il club. Da questo momento in poi sarò con voi, dagli spalti, a tifare per i ragazzi".

#2245. Frattesi, Mancini: «uno dei migliori per rendimento» alla Lazio

Prima di Italia-Francia, il ct lega il momento del centrocampista alla continuità trovata nella squadra di Gattuso.

Roberto Mancini elogia Davide Frattesi alla vigilia di Italia-Francia, sfida di Nations League in programma allo stadio Giuseppe Meazza di Milano. Il commissario tecnico azzurro indica il centrocampista della Lazio tra i giocatori dal rendimento migliore in questo momento. Ai microfoni della Rai parla anche della partita e delle esclusioni di Liberali e Cisse.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Nel presentare la sfida, Mancini si sofferma sul periodo del centrocampista biancoceleste. Frattesi sta trovando spazio con continuità nella Lazio allenata da Gennaro Gattuso e ha assunto un ruolo importante negli equilibri della squadra. Il ct collega proprio alla regolarità d’impiego i progressi dell’ex giocatore dell’Inter.

«Frattesi sta giocando con continuità alla Lazio, quindi ha trovato probabilmente la sua identità. Sta bene, gioca, è tranquillo. In questo momento sicuramente è uno dei migliori per rendimento». Le parole di Mancini accompagnano l’avvicinamento del centrocampista all’impegno con la Nazionale, dopo le prestazioni offerte in maglia biancoceleste.

A poche ore dall’incontro con la Francia, Mancini richiama l’attenzione sulla prova che chiede agli Azzurri. Il ct vuole che la squadra giochi bene e ottenga un buon risultato, anche per non deludere i tifosi. Sottolinea inoltre la risposta del pubblico quando la Nazionale scende in campo a San Siro.

«Dovremo fare una bella partita perché altrimenti i tifosi ci rimarranno male. Dovremo cercare di giocare bene e fare un buon risultato. E comunque San Siro fa sempre il pieno quando arriva la Nazionale». È questa l’aspettativa espressa dal selezionatore per la sfida con i francesi, nella quale Frattesi punta a confermare in azzurro quanto mostrato con la Lazio.

Mancini chiarisce anche la scelta di lasciare fuori Liberali e Cisse dall’elenco dei calciatori disponibili per la partita. I due giovani sono tra gli ultimi arrivati nel gruppo e il commissario tecnico richiama sia l’impegno previsto tra tre giorni sia il numero dei giocatori presenti.

«È una scelta perché comunque sono gli ultimi arrivati e abbiamo una partita tra tre giorni. Quindi oggi è stata questa la scelta. Siamo in 28 e purtroppo qualcuno deve andare in tribuna». L’esclusione dei due calciatori rientra così, nelle parole di Mancini, nella gestione del gruppo in vista degli impegni ravvicinati.

#2244. Some are calling this 'Tuchel 2.0' and his latest squad does feel like that. Here's why England think a tilt at the European Championship is within reach, writes IAN LADYMAN

Published: 17:35 EST, 6 November 2026 | Updated: 05:45 EST, 9 November 2026

One of Thomas Tuchel’s favourite analogies when it comes to the development of his England team is that of a train leaving a station with only the chosen few on it. As time moves on, the bodies lying on the tracks are growing greater in number.

Consider this statistic. Of the 26 players who travelled to the World Cup in America 13 are not in the squad chosen by England manager Tuchel for next week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain. And that does not include Cole Palmer and Phil Foden who, after missing out in the summer, were expected by many of us to have forced a way back in by now.

Tuchel’s latest selection has been affected by injuries, of course. But more significant is that the experienced German believes he is now starting to see an England team and squad develop in a way and in a direction that even he hadn’t envisaged once Argentina ended his World Cup hopes in that dismal Atlanta semi-final in July.

Different feelings, different style of play and, to a degree, different players.

Some are calling this ‘Tuchel 2.0’ and it does feel a little bit like that. The start of the second phase of Tuchel’s tenure, the start of the road towards a tilt at another trophy, the European Championships of 2028.

Having admitted to some worry ahead of the four-game international break FIFA saddled us all with last month, Tuchel sat down yesterday looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself.

Tuchel sat down with the media looking and sounding like a man once again certain of himself

The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham — Jude’s younger brother (right) — was the headline act but there were other messages written within

Certain enough of a direct, quick, athletic style of play that helped England to two wins over Czech Republic and one – by seven goals – against Croatia in Rijeka. And certain that a dependence on players like Jordan Henderson, Dan Burn and John Stones for what we may politely call ‘squad culture management’ lies now in the past.

All of this may crash down in Madrid next Sunday. Spain have already beaten Tuchel’s England once – at Wembley in late September – and a repeat this month would ask familiar questions about England against the really good teams.

But for now, Tuchel is confident enough to claim that he has found his path.

‘We said at some point we need to take the next step, to build on what we have, to get better and to improve otherwise you’re just left behind,’ said Tuchel yesterday.

‘That’s how football works. You have been champion in one season but you need to improve, you need to bring in new players for competition, young players, new energy, fresh energy. It’s also the way, naturally, the national team goes.

‘We cannot be stuck in the same personnel and in the same style of play.

‘I agreed with you last month. I was the first to admit I was not 100 per cent happy with the pure level of football we played in the US. I saw a higher level in training [than on the field], I saw a higher level in glimpses.

‘We adjusted some things tactically, created some new positions and took the next steps.’

The Tuchel we sat down with in late September still wore the scars of the summer’s disappointment – and the criticism that came with it – rather visibly. It was the first time we had seen him like that in his two years in the job. He was tetchy and easily provoked. Call it the Argentina effect if you like.

Here, he appeared rather healed. Good results tend to do that for a manager and a little time helps too. If he believes his team has moved on then maybe he has also and he had to.

Certainly, his selection squad speaks to that. The inclusion of Jobe Bellingham – Jude’s younger brother – was the headline act but there were other messages written within.

Henderson and Burn are available but not included. So too Arsenal’s Noni Madueke, excluded to the benefit of the more direct Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha.

‘We need runners who will go between the lines,’ said Tuchel. A clear indication, there, that too much of England’s summer wing play was too slow and too conservatively narrow.

Palmer, Foden and Kobbie Mainoo are also on the outside looking in once again and the case of the Manchester United midfielder is perhaps indicative of how Tuchel now operates.

Moved to apologise to him in front of the whole squad in July for his lack of minutes at the World Cup, Tuchel was determined Mainoo would play in the opening four games of the Nations League campaign.

‘I was desperate to give him the minutes and desperate to include him in this new start,’ explained Tuchel.

‘But then he pulled out. He missed an excellent camp and also entered a difficult, difficult spell for himself.

‘Man United fell off a cliff a little bit performance-wise. So this is why he now suffers.’

We can talk about the whys and wherefores of that logic. If Mainoo was good enough in September then why is he not good enough now? How desperate could Tuchel really have been to play him that one withdrawal with injury closed the door for the next camp and opened it instead for Bellingham jnr?

This, though, is how Tuchel works. He is an adept tactician but he’s also a mood coach, someone who – after sobering club experiences at places like PSG, Chelsea and Bayern Munich – places huge emphasis on environments and gut feels and culture. If he feels something works, he doesn’t like to pick it apart without good reason.

This is why for example the growing voice and influence of Elliot Anderson has left Jordan Henderson suddenly surplus. Tuchel says the door is not closed on a player who will be 38 by the time the next Euros are played and he called him this week to say so. In Tuchel’s mind, though, England will now move without the veteran and others of his ilk.

‘I was concerned before the last camp that we missed the players who kept our standards,’ said Tuchel.

‘I was worried that we missed so many of them. But then this group found their own way and their own voices.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game changing duo of Palmer and Foden

‘I know what the others did. They built a platform on which these ones can build.’

Time will tell. To a degree, Spain will tell. Can England play the kind of higher tempo, front foot football we saw against Croatia and the Czechs against the world and European champions next Sunday? They embarrassed us when we didn’t have the ball at Wembley.

It’s also reasonable to ask why our head coach can’t find room in his squad – if not his team – for the game-changing duo of Palmer and Foden. England lacked good substitutes at the World Cup. There was too much like for like.

England need to win in order for such decisions to be vindicated and Tuchel knows that.

Asked yesterday if he felt as invigorated as he looked he said he did. ‘The last camp gave me a lot of energy, gave me a lot of extra belief,’ he said.

‘It gave me a lot of optimism to not compromise on the way England teams should play. Be physical but also step up in the pure level of performances.’

It’s certainly time for this now. The summer only served to expose English shortcomings. Tuchel’s train must arrive in Madrid next weekend, not only with fresh personnel but also new ideas clearly apparent.

#2242. Tare pungente su Pulisic: "Mi aspettavo qualcosa in più a livello di responsabilità e di leadership"

Igli Tare, ex Direttore Sportivo del Milan, è stato protagonista dell’ultimo episodio di Sky Calcio Unplugged con Gianluca Di Marzio, Stefano Borghi e Fayna. Queste le sue dichiarazioni a 360° sull'esperienza in rossonero: dai colpi di mercato alla grande delusione di non andare in Champions, fino ad alcune dinamiche societarie e al rapporto con Gerry Cardinale. Ecco quindi un interessante estratto delle sue parole sul rendimento di alcuni giocatori rossoneri nella passata stagione. Che steccata a Christian Pulisic:

“La sensazione che ho avuto all’inizio è che un po’ mancasse questa leadership. L’arrivo di Modric - e un altro nostro obiettivo era anche Granit Xhaka, capitano del Leverkusen - era proprio per portare in un gruppo giocatori veri, con caratteristiche importanti e capaci di guidare gli altri. Granit non è arrivato, è arrivato Luka che ha un altro modo di essere leader: lo è in silenzio e con il suo atteggiamento in campo. Ho avuto modo di conoscere Mike Maignan: un ragazzo straordinario, un’anima che ci tiene tanto alla maglia del Milan. Gabbia un altro ragazzo straordinario, vive per questo club. Anche Rabiot… La sua esperienza parlava da sé. Il grande dispiacere è che mi aspettavo qualcosa in più a livello di responsabilità e di leadership da Pulisic: è un giocatore di grande livello che ha qualità indiscutibili. Ma in termini di rendimento sono successe delle cose che non avevo mai vissuto nella mia carriera… Come Gimenez: un ragazzo straordinario con numeri che parlavano da sé per un anno non è riuscito a segnare un gol. Poi è capitato che Pulisic per sei mesi non ha segnato un gol. Poi Leao che non ha segnato per 4 mesi. Sono successe situazioni che difficilmente trovi nel mondo del calcio… Capita che non riesci a segnare per un mese, due mesi, ma così a lungo ha inciso anche nel rendimento finale della squadra. Perdere una partita col Cagliari come l’abbiamo persa, 2-1, penso che per me è stata la partita più brutta della mia vita. La sensazione e il dispiacere che ho sentito nei confronti dei tifosi allo stadio quella sera non me la scorderò mai per tutta la mia vita”.

Inter dominante: cosa dicono gli Expected Goals. È il dato migliore in A. La squadra di Chivu...

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

In Serie A quasi sempre l'Inter è dominante. I nerazzurri riescono a schiacciare l'avversario in area per lunghi tratti della gara. Come sottolinea la Gazzetta dello Sport, questa sensazione ha trovato conferma anche negli Expected Goals, ovvero i gol attesi, o gol potenziali, calcolati in base alla qualità delle occasioni. L’Inter ha quasi rispettato alla lettera questi dati, raccogliendo leggermente meno di quanto avrebbe dovuto.

"Nelle prime 11 giornate i nerazzurri sono a 29 Expected Goals (il dato migliore delle 20 squadre di Serie A) e nella pratica l’hanno buttata dentro 28 volte (Chivu è primo anche per i tiri in porta: 76). Un’aderenza quasi perfetta fra realtà e virtuale. Segno che la mira dei nerazzurri in campionato è abbastanza precisa, mentre in Europa va in maniera leggermente diversa".

"Lo si è visto nella prova di forza contro il Como, domenica scorsa: in Italia, la squadra di Cristian Chivu si sente padrona di sé e del campo, ha una sicurezza - oltre a una qualità della rosa - che le avversarie non hanno. E tutto questo si traduce anche nella freddezza sotto porta. La Roma invece ha addirittura “overperformato”, ha concretizzando più di quanto avrebbe dovuto secondo le statistiche. I giallorossi hanno 26,3 come dato di Expetced Goals, secondo valore del campionato, e nella realtà hanno segnato ben 31 gol. Anche il Frosinone - non è una novità - è una squadra che attacca con qualità e infatti è al terzo posto come xG con 20,3: i gol segnati dai ragazzi di Massimiliano Alvini sono stati 24".

#2239. Inside Cristiano Ronaldo Jr's bid to step out of his father's shadow after his Portugal Under-17s call-up: From padel beef with Rio Ferdinand to a Coca-Cola BAN

Published: 02:00 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 05:50 EST, 9 November 2026

He has spent his whole life being measured against European football's greatest goalscorer. Now Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. has taken his biggest step yet.

The 16-year-old has been called up to Portugal's U17 squad for the first time, and will face Andorra on November 11 and Serbia on November 14. And the timing is hard to ignore.

The famous No. 7 shirt Ronaldo Sr wore for two decades will now be vacant after he announced his retirement from international football on Thursday.

It's a heavy shirt for anyone to inherit. Luis Figo graced the number when he led Portugal’s golden generation to the 2006 World Cup semi-finals, and Ronaldo Sr himself carried it when he captained them to the European Championship in 2016. Both won the Ballon d’Or and are two of the most tantalising players the nation has ever produced.

Portugal’s power vacuum is also a pressure point. As the son of the man who wore that shirt, Ronaldo Jr. will attract more attention, and more expectation.

The national team lacks its focal point, and few names carry more weight than his. He is the natural successor in marketing terms, if nothing else. Whether he is the player to take it is another matter.

Cristiano Ronaldo Jr - son of the Portuguese great - is looking to forge his own football career

This week the 16-year-old earned his first call-up to Portugal's U17 team

The weight of his father's expectations has been there from the start. Ronaldo Jr once floated the idea of becoming a goalkeeper, and his father’s reaction was swift. “No, I don’t want that! Are you joking or what?” Ronaldo Sr responds in the 2015 documentary Ronaldo.

Up front for the Juventus academy, his record would make the man chasing 1,000 career goals jealous: a staggering 58 goals in 23 games for the Under-9s. Yet his father was never satisfied. Asked at the 2020 Globe Soccer Awards, with his son sitting in the audience, whether the boy had what it takes to reach the top, Ronaldo Sr’s answer was blunt.

“Not yet,” he said. “I’m hard with him sometimes because he drinks Coca-Cola and Fanta. (He has) chips and fries; I fight with him.”

Hard data on his youth career since then is limited. Reports of his interest in switching to the Real Madrid academy suggested a desire to develop and compete.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Ronaldo Sr. at Manchester United, has seen that competitive streak in the son on the padel court.

“I was in the Red Sea a couple of days ago; I play padel every day. (When) me and Cristiano Jr. get mad, we don't speak for like two days.” He exclaimed on Five Presents. Like his father, he doesn’t take losing well.

His body, though, has settled the question of position. At 6 ft 3 in, he already stands taller than his father. Growth spurts may temporarily cost him some of the pace and the effortless coordination of his youth. A forced adaption of his style is not unusual: Ronaldo’s former teammates Gareth Bale and Scott McTominay were both moved into new positions to begin their professional careers.

It is also a path his father walked. Forget stepovers, flicks and trademark ‘Ronaldo chop’. Jr’s game is currently closer to the Ronaldo of Juventus and the Old Trafford return: a penalty-box predator who lives on timing and movement rather than dribbling past defenders.

The young striker has represented the youth academies of Man United, Real Madrid and Juventus

But his ultra-professional father said his son needs to cut out the Coca-Cola if he wants to make it at the top level

His Portugal numbers are respectable, not remarkable. Five goals in 13 appearances is a decent return, but he has played just 522 minutes, an average of around 40 per game, and scored roughly once every 104 minutes. However, it is a tiny sample size.

To reach the top, he will need the work ethic his father is famous for. “I’ve never seen a more professional person,” Paul Scholes, Ronaldo Sr’s former Manchester United teammate, told Premier League Productions. “He was out there all day long, practising … he had weights on his ankles.”

Habits like that are built in demanding environments, and Jr’s has been a gentle one.

Playing in Saudi Arabia still has its positives. As Jr. transitions from boy to man, weaker opposition has given him room to grow into his body and build confidence as he prepares for men's senior football. But that breathing space has a shelf life.

He has options. He could stay and share a dressing room with his father, or return to one of the academies of Ronaldo Sr’s former clubs, with Real Madrid, Juventus and Manchester United all reported by The Sun to be interested. He has the name, the call-up and the options, but not yet the proof.

When Ronaldo Sr walked away from Portugal, he left behind a shirt, a record and a question. Saudi Arabia cannot give his son the answer. If he wants international caps and Champions League football, he must leave Al Nassr and his old man for a stage where nobody gives him an inch.

The surname opened the door. Only he can walk through it.

#2234. Giornata mondiale della gentilezza: il settore giovanile del Milan celebra il fair play attraverso l'esempio di Franco Baresi

In occasione della Giornata Mondiale della Gentilezza, che si celebra il 13 novembre, tutti i giovani giocatori e le giovani giocatrici del Milan hanno ricevuto una lettera speciale dedicata ai valori del rispetto, della solidarietà e del fair play, attraverso la storia e l'esempio di Franco Baresi. L'iniziativa, promossa dall'Area Psicologica del Settore Giovanile rossonero, nasce con l'obiettivo di sensibilizzare atleti e atlete sull'importanza della gentilezza nello sport e nella vita quotidiana, ricordando come il rispetto e l'attenzione verso gli altri siano elementi fondamentali nella crescita personale e sportiva.

Protagonista della lettera è la storia dello storico Capitano del Milan, Franco Baresi, simbolo di leadership, correttezza e senso di appartenenza. Attraverso il racconto della sua esperienza, vengono ripercorsi gli insegnamenti ricevuti fin da bambino, in oratorio e dai suoi allenatori, che gli hanno trasmesso il valore del rispetto, dell'educazione, del sacrificio e dell'attenzione verso gli altri. "La gentilezza è anche non lasciare indietro nessuno" è il messaggio che accompagna la testimonianza di Baresi, ricordando che essere capitano non significa soltanto rappresentare un punto di riferimento tecnico, ma anche assumersi la responsabilità di sostenere e valorizzare i propri compagni.

La lettera invita quindi a riflettere sul significato concreto della gentilezza all'interno di una squadra: "Significa accorgersi di un compagno che è in difficoltà, incoraggiarlo dopo un errore, aiutare chi sta imparando, rispettare chi è diverso da noi e saper riconoscere il valore degli altri, anche quando sono nostri avversari." Un messaggio che sottolinea come la gentilezza non sia in contrasto con lo spirito competitivo, ma rappresenti un valore aggiunto per chiunque pratichi sport: "La gentilezza non ci rende meno determinati e non ci impedisce di voler vincere. Ci insegna a farlo senza dimenticarci umiltà, correttezza e attenzione verso le persone."

L'iniziativa si inserisce nel percorso educativo del Settore Giovanile del Milan, che affianca alla formazione sportiva la trasmissione di valori fondamentali per la crescita degli atleti e delle atlete. La lettera si conclude con una riflessione che racchiude il senso dell'iniziativa: "Perché una squadra forte non è quella in cui nessuno ha bisogno degli altri, ma quella in cui nessuno viene lasciato solo."

#2231. Napoli, l’ass.Cosenza: “Stadio Maradona? Alte probabilità per Euro 2032. Il cantiere aprirà nel 2028”

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio è intervenuto l’assessore alle infrastrutture Edoardo Cosenza: “L’allarme bomba inviato alle scuole italiane? Difficile capire se l’email inviate agli istituti siano effettive. Però per principi di sicurezza, capisco che si sia reagito in questo modo. Non sono scherzi da ragazzi. Bisogna capire cosa ci sia dietro. Napoli città ospitante per EURO 2032? La data limite di fine ottobre per scoprire se la città avrebbe ospitato gli Europei era stata data dall’UEFA, ma da parecchio tempo avevo intuito che si sarebbe andato oltre. Di Napoli parlano benissimo, come parlano benissimo di altre città. Gli incontri con UEFA e Abodi sono andati benissimo. La probabilità che la città ospiti gli Europei è alta. Le grandi città come Milano, Roma e Napoli hanno un forte vantaggio competitivo. Così come Torino. Ci sono fibrillazioni in altre città come Milano per l’abbattimento di San Siro, ma qui non ci sono problemi. Sono due anni che stiamo lavorando per questo. Quando un’opera supera i 50 milioni di euro, deve avere l’ok del Consiglio Superiore dei lavori pubblici. Questo non comporta l’allungamento dei tempi, la procedura si risolverà entro fine gennaio. La delibera Cipess dovrà essere deliberata dalla Corte dei Conti. A quel punto, il nostro progetto sarà ancora più affidabile. Sul terzo anello dello stadio Maradona si va avanti, ma anche per la riqualificazione dei parcheggi. Quando lo stadio Maradona diventerà un cantiere? Se la gara la faremo partire nel primo trimestre del 2027, con conclusione attorno alla metà del 2027, allora poi servirà il progetto esecutivo. Dall’inizio del 2028 saremo pronti per l’inizio dei lavori. Il nostro primo obiettivo è mettere a posto il terzo anello, per non ridurre la capienza dello stadio. Quando faremo i lavori per il primo anello, garantiremo la possibilità di andare al terzo anello. Non si andrà mai meno dei 54 mila posti attuali. Le prime prove le avremo nel breve. In funzione dei lavori al primo anello, apriremo poi il terzo anello. Il terzo anello lo apriremo man mano che ci servirà, ma i lavori inizieranno certamente prima dei lavori al primo anello dello stadio Maradona”.

#2229. Forest Green apologise for failing to commemorate Remembrance Day at a home match due to 'mistake'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 10:15 EST, 8 November 2026 | Updated: 07:03 EST, 9 November 2026

Forest Green Rovers have apologised for failing to commemorate Remembrance Day at a home game, labelling it as 'human error' and a 'mistake' from the club.

Remembrance Day is November 11 with Forest Green's sole fixture around that date having been Saturday's 2-0 FA Cup first-round defeat at Luton Town. Both teams commemorated the occasion ahead of kick-off at Kenilworth Road.

Forest Green's last home fixture prior to that was a 2-2 draw with Harrogate Town on October 31 in the National League.

That encounter at The New Lawn saw supporters of the fifth-tier side take to a fan forum post-match questioning why nothing was in place for Remembrance Day - due to their then-forthcoming clash with Luton being an away tie.

Forest Green CEO Dane Vince replied on the club's Fan Advisory Board, admitting it was an oversight on their part.

'The lack of Remembrance at a home game is simply down to a human error/mistake on the club,' he wrote.

Forest Green Rovers have apologised for not commemorating Remembrance Day at a home game (National League side pictured doing so during Saturday's FA Cup 2-0 defeat at Luton)

Forest Green failed to do so in their home draw vs Harrogate on October 31, calling it a 'mistake'

Vince continued that a condensed schedule in this period didn't help matters, but still acknowledged that the club should have done more.

'It didn't help that we had a sizable number of games in a small time frame (including the FA Cup replay) beforehand; albeit that isn't an excuse, we should have got this right.'

Following the incident, Vince confirmed that Forest Green would contact the Royal British Legion for advice on future commemorations to ensure this wouldn't happen again. He also underlined that the missed home commemoration did not signal any change in the club's support for Remembrance or the Royal British Legion.

'This was a simple error/mistake,' he reiterated.

Una serata emozionante, forse la doppietta con l’Ucraina serviva per un altro scopo però far gol qui è sempre speciale perché in quella porta c’è stato il gol più importante della mia carriera e sono contento di aver segnato questa sera, in questa notte bellissima.

Lazio e Nazionale? Sono due situazioni analoghe, nella Lazio, nonostante la prima sconfitta, siamo riusciti a compattarci e a trovare entusiasmo, credo che quella sia la cosa più importante anche qui grazie al mister e ai ragazzi nuovi che hanno portato una ventata d’aria fresca. Quando c’è un ambiente sano è tutto più facile. Io più che per la vittoria sono contento per il carattere e l’abnegazione che c’è stata.

Con Gattuso abbiamo qualche discussione perché mi chiede di esaltare le caratteristiche che ho, io invece vorrei fare al 100% quello che non so fare. Però quello è sempre stato il mio obiettivo, levarmi le etichette che non rispecchiano quello che sono davvero. Sono contento di aver fiducia da Gattuso e da Mancini.

Quando riesco ad avere quei 10-15 metri e riesco ad accelerare in corsa riesco a coprire una porzione di campo più grande. Come oggi che sono arrivato dietro al difensore, mi sono staccato e ho fatto gol. Per me è importante arrivare da dietro in corsa perché così io posso decidere come attaccare.

Gol contro il Napoli? Quello è merito di Gattuso che ci massacra durante la settimana, la forma fisica c'è.

Mancini? Dopp il gol stavamo parlando della fase difensiva.

#2223. Xabi Alonso was brought in to end the chaos at Chelsea and he is failing. PLUS: Football's most vanilla pundit gives out-of-his-depth Michael Carrick an easy ride: IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

Published: 07:00 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 07:55 EST, 9 November 2026

The whiff of Premier League failure is in the air as the smoke clears from Bonfire Night.

It always feels this way by the time we get to the November international break.

Managers and their players have had time to settle in and teething problems no longer cut it as a reason for autumn struggles.

Worst of all, Christmas is coming and we all know what tends to happen to teams who are struggling as the end of the year nears.

So at places like Manchester United, Crystal Palace, Sunderland, Newcastle and Spurs there is anxiety about expectations not being met.

Xabi Alonso was hired to break the cycle at Chelsea and he is not yet succeeding

Xabi Alonso's side would appear to be the team that is failing without anybody seeming to notice.

At Stamford Bridge, the environment is conducive to Alonso and his team doing well this season.

Chelsea – not in Europe after last season's troubles – are only playing once a week. So Alonso – hired for his coaching reputation – has time on the grass with players who should arrive every weekend with freshness in their legs.

It's the environment that enabled Michael Carrick to fool everyone at Manchester United last season. While the rest of the Premier League got bogged down in the schedule, United sailed upwards on the back of a lighter load.

When we look at Alonso's team we see only familiar Chelsea things – and not in a good way.

Inconsistent tactics, some strange selections and, on the back of it, some very ordinary results.

This is the cycle Alonso was hired to break and he is not yet succeeding.

Sunday's defeat to Sunderland can be added to league setbacks against Spurs, Brentford and Arsenal.

They were unimpressive in beating United a couple of weeks ago also. Carrick's team outplayed them in the first half and should have been two or three goals ahead.

Under Alonso, Chelsea are yet to establish an identity or discernible patterns. It is hard to know yet what his best back four (or five) looks like. In the absence of the injured striker Joao Pedro, Alonso seems happier to play without one rather than use Danny Welbeck, signed for just this scenario in the summer.

The absence of Joao Pedro is significant while Alonso is also without his first choice goalkeeper Emi Martinez. These things matter.

But Chelsea have a huge squad of international players. Maybe it's too big. Whatever the case Alonso must get the best out of it soon.

Nobody seems to be talking about how very underwhelming the whole thing feels. But if it continues, they soon will be.

On Match of the Day on Sunday night, football's most vanilla pundit Dion Dublin was asked whether Michael Carrick has done enough to keep his job.

'I think so,' said Dublin. 'I think Michael has all the tools but the players just aren't doing what they need to do.'

At every other club in the Premier League, under-performing players and the bad results that tend to follow lead to intense scrutiny and criticism of the manager. It's his job to affect these things.

Not at United, though, where the level of public and media support for Carrick remains extraordinary and illogical.

If we applied this level of leeway to everybody else then nobody would ever be sacked.

Dion Dublin, pictured on Homes Under The Hammer duty, gave Michael Carrick an easy ride

Carrick is out of his depth at sinking Manchester United - his team are a shambles

Yes, there are a number of factors at play at Old Trafford. Yes, we know what they are and who is to blame for them. Yes, it's a very difficult job.

But the truth is that Carrick is failing in a quite spectacular fashion.

Of all the managers to have followed Sir Alex Ferguson over the last 13 and a half years, Erik ten Hag was the one who looked most out of his depth in terms of the chaotic nature of his team's football.

Carrick is now on the way to eclipsing that. His team are a shambles and that's on him. Once again, this is a mediocre league and it's quite criminal that Carrick has his group of players in the bottom three.

The former Middlesbrough manager is so out of his depth it's quite painful to watch.

It was another extraordinary afternoon at Old Trafford as United drew 4-4 with Aston Villa.

Unai Emery's Villa team is going through yet another regeneration after the sale of big-name players in the summer and balancing the Champions League with domestic football will once again be a challenge.

Emery seems to have made his mind up about one of his squad members, though, after former United and Chelsea winger Alejandro Garnacho was left out of the squad entirely yesterday.

Garnacho is a talented player but has made only 14 Premier League starts – and none at Villa – since leaving Old Trafford for Chelsea in the summer of 2025.

The Argentine is still only 22 so time is on his side but at some point he is going to have to do something on the field to justify the investment in a career that is currently going nowhere.

Alejandro Garnacho was left out of the squad entirely yesterday by Aston Villa

Sky's excellent touchline reporter Patrick Davison had his work cut out post-match at Old Trafford as he interviewed one manager in danger of the sack and another who had just flounced down the tunnel like a chap with his pants on fire.

Neither Michael Carrick nor Unai Emery seemed particularly comfortable in the face of Davison's questions and that's exactly as it should be.

He is there to ask questions on behalf of a broadcaster that ploughs billions of pounds into our national sport each year. He is not there to apply soothing balm.

There would appear to be many others happy to do that anyway.

Sky's Patrick Davison (right) is not there to apply soothing balm with his questions

Less impressive was the appearance of Sky's latest metric that appeared on screen during Nottingham Forest's dismantling of Manchester City on Saturday.

Titled simply 'pressures' it indicated that Forest were doing rather better at it than City.

But what did it mean? Does anybody know? Or indeed care?

Two seasons ago at the City Ground I saw local boy Ryan Yates give Casemiro such a chasing as Forest beat Manchester United that the great Brazilian was taken off before he was sent off.

On Saturday by the river, Yates made his first league start of the season as Oliver Glasner’s team overwhelmed City.

Beforehand Yates gave an address to his team-mates. He told them about what it meant to play for the club and touched briefly on its history.

He told me once in an interview that he tends to tell all new arrivals at Forest what the two stars on the shirt actually mean – two European Cups won in 1979 and 1980.

It’s smart work by a lad who knows what football means in Nottingham and it was smart work by his manager who knew that his team needed an injection of something visceral to drag him from a trough of failure that was threatening to cost him his job.

Manchester United could probably do with a bit of that right now. So, possibly, could Chelsea and indeed Tottenham. At Liverpool, they lament the absence from the team of Trent Alexander-Arnold and Curtis Jones.

It takes an awful lot to make up a Premier League team these days. Place of birth is not a priority any more and that’s understandable. But sometimes it helps.

When was the last time an English team won the title with a poor goalkeeper?

Flick back over the last couple of decades and it's hard to find an example.

So what hope for Manchester City this season?

Gianluigi Donnarumma is anything but a poor goalkeeper but the problem is that he is playing like one and it is there that City's current problems start.

Enzo Maresca's back four looks shot to pieces and that often happens when they lose faith in the chap behind them.

Maresca says he won't change. 'My team is Gigi plus ten others,' is his take.

Enzo Maresca says he will not change goalkeeper despite Gianluigi Donnarumma's problems

His back up is 34-year-old Argentinean Geronimo Rulli, a member of his country's World Cup squad with nine caps to his name.

Rulli is well-travelled and has some pedigree. He was, for example, Villarreal's hero as they beat Manchester United in a Europa League final shoot out in 2021.

If Maresca trusts him then maybe now is the time to show it. If he doesn't then why did City sign him?

Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson is perhaps not quite what he once was at the age of 34 but produced a throwback performance for his team at Crystal Palace. Without him, Liverpool would not have won.

Nevertheless Palace's struggles go on and their coach Pierre Sage is in danger of losing his job.

However the south London club cannot say they were not warned about trouble ahead.

Former manager Oliver Glasner spent most of last season in a huff about what he saw as a failure by the Palace board to invest properly in the squad.

Palace have won twice in ten Premier League games this season and it seems Glasner may have been right.

Brighton continue to fly high and to produce such an energetic performance to beat Brentford having played away at Getafe in Europe on Thursday was testimony to the fitness of Fabian Hurzeler's squad.

The Seagulls were certainly helped by having to play against ten for an hour, though, and on Match of the Day the enduringly listenable Jonathan Pearce spoke for all of us as he watched Chema Andres go down after minimal contact to his cheek from Brentford's Igor Thiago.

'That was nothing, nothing, nothing,' said Pearce as Thiago walked off.

Coming so soon after theatrics from Alexis MacAllister and Gabriel in the Liverpool-Arsenal game last week, the issue of players exaggerating facial contact to get opponents sent off remains a live one.

Brentford's manager Keith Andrews was measured on the issue but suggested the tactic was becoming 'a game within a game'.

It's a problem and referees head Howard Webb needs his officials to get a grip of it.

Brighton's Pascal Gross has now created more than 25 chances for team-mates this season and that's more than anyone else in the Premier League.

Gross cost £1.2million when he returned to the club from Borussia Dortmund last January.

It constitutes another steal in the market by Brighton's stat boffins but this time they probably didn't need the data to convince them of its merits.

Pascal Gross scored on Sunday and has now created more than 25 chances for team-mates

Bournemouth, meanwhile, cast their net as widely as anybody these days and that includes all the way down the English pyramid.

The South Coast club – on an eight-match winning streak now under Marco Rose – have a relationship with yesterday's FA Cup giant killers Wimborne from the seventh tier.

Wimborne of the Southern League Premier South beat League Two Crawley in Round One and will this week send their Chilean teenage striker Angel Diaz for a trial at the Premier League club.

Story of last season in the EFL was probably Lincoln City's promotion to the Championship where, after 15 games, they are just about keeping their heads above water in 21st place.

Architect of that incredible rise was former futsal coach Michael Skubala who rather sullied the romantic feel of it all by quitting almost immediately to join Bristol City.

This weekend Skubala's team were thrashed 5-0 at home by Norwich with the home fans singing that their manager would be 'sacked in the morning'.

Lincoln have already won at Ashton Gate, back in September, at the start of a run that has seen City win just two from ten.

Sometimes, it really does pay just to stay where you are.

#2220. Frosinone, Zerbin: "Alvini, un po' di Conte e un po' di Spalletti. Andrebbe in guerra per noi"

Al rientro dalla sosta, fra poco più di una settimana, il Milan riprenderà la sua stagione a San Siro con un impegno da non sottovalutare, per non dire molto ostico. Il commento di Alessio Zerbin sul grande inizio di stagione del Frosinone: "Nel mister Alvini vedo un po' di Conte e di Spalletti, per l'allenamento, per la passione e per la ricerca del dettaglio. Non è banale, ci fa vedere anche un passaggio sbagliato di mezzo metro ed è una cosa che fanno anche Conte e Spalletti. Ci tratta come fossimo i suoi figli, andrebbe in guerra per noi. Col Frosinone ci divertiamo tantissimo. Durante la settimana ci facciamo il mazzo, ma abbiamo capito che seguendo il mister possiamo divertirci. #2219. Mauro: «La Lazio è una meravigliosa realtà», ma l’Inter è favorita

L’ex calciatore non si sbilancia sullo scudetto biancoceleste e considera una sorpresa anche l’eventuale successo della Roma.

Massimo Mauro elogia la Lazio di Gattuso e non esclude che una squadra romana possa sorprendere nella corsa allo scudetto. Secondo quanto riportato da La Gazzetta dello Sport, Per l’ex calciatore l’Inter resta la più forte, ma il rendimento dei biancocelesti nelle prime undici giornate merita attenzione: «La Lazio è una meravigliosa realtà, una grande sorpresa. Le va riconosciuto e lo faccio con grande piacere».

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Mauro considera il cammino biancoceleste più di una buona partenza. Collega i risultati al lavoro di Gattuso e cita tre giocatori: «Siamo quasi a un terzo di Serie A e Gattuso ha fatto dare il 120% a diversi giocatori: Isaksen, Taylor, Noslin... La qualità è veramente elevata, queste prime 11 partite non sono un caso».

Sullo scudetto, però, distingue l’apprezzamento per la Lazio da un pronostico: «Non me la sento di dire che lotterà per lo scudetto, ma mi farebbe molto piacere se ci fosse una grande sorpresa: potrebbe essere che lo scudetto lo vince una romana e non l’Inter».

Nel suo ragionamento rientra anche la Roma di Gasperini, che continua a reggere nonostante l’infortunio di Dybala e altri problemi: «È l’altra realtà che mi sta piacendo di più, perché regge nonostante l’infortunio di Dybala e qualche altra tegola».

Mauro ne individua la forza nella scelta di non cambiare modo di giocare, neppure quando è avanti nel punteggio: «Regge perché Gasperini manda a quel paese chi gli dice di gestire, di non giocare alla Garibaldina, di snaturare la sua realtà quando vince 2-0: chi solleva queste critiche non capisce che la Roma riesce a reggere i primi posti proprio perché ha la mentalità giusta che deriva anche dal giocare sempre nella stessa maniera. Se si tirasse indietro diventerebbe un’altra cosa, non riuscirebbe a fare quanto fatto fino a ora».

L’Inter rimane il riferimento nella valutazione di Mauro. Sugli alti e bassi dei nerazzurri dice: «Li hanno risolti molto bene, perché l’unico scivolone grosso è stato col Milan. L’Inter è la più forte e se regge nei punti chiave dovrebbe vincere con 10 punti di vantaggio sulla seconda».

Mauro indica Calhanoglu, Lautaro, Thuram, Bastoni, Barella e Dimarco come i giocatori decisivi per la tenuta della squadra: «Però Calhanoglu, Lautaro, Thuram, Bastoni, Barella e Dimarco devono tenere il livello altissimo di questi ultimi anni. Se questi giocatori continuano ad avere la mentalità vincente, l’Inter arriva fino in fondo dappertutto perché ha un grande organico».

C’è però un aspetto che giudica negativamente, legato alla dirigenza: «La perdita di Ausilio. È vero che i dirigenti non fanno i gol, però chi sa fare il proprio lavoro di direttore sportivo mantiene l’equilibrio all’interno dello spogliatoio, nei rapporti tra la società, i giocatori e gli agenti: contratti, decisioni, chi va a parametro zero, chi vendi, chi compri... Ausilio è un maestro. L’Inter un po’ di problemini li ha avuti, forse la perdita di Ausilio è stata un errore, visto quello che l’Inter ha ottenuto con lui. Vedremo, lo dirà il futuro».

Il giudizio su Milan e Juventus è meno favorevole. Mauro descrive un rendimento che cambia da una settimana all’altra: «Sono indecifrabili. Pensi che hanno risolto i problemi e la settimana dopo sprofondano di nuovo. Non sai cosa dire quando le vedi giocare come il Milan in Europa League e la Juve a Cagliari o contro il Sassuolo. Le sconfitte sono già pesantissime, per quante sono e per come sono arrivate».

Nel motivare il giudizio, Mauro confronta le prestazioni a cui ha assistito e torna sul problema della continuità: «Ero a Juventus-Lazio e sembravano una squadra di Serie A contro una di Serie C. Poi però ci sono stati Juventus-Napoli e il derby di Milano... Dall’esterno si può dire che non sono grandi squadre perché non hanno continuità: le grandi squadre reggono l’alto livello di prestazioni, loro no. Significa che fino adesso si è costruito male. Il Milan ha forse qualche centrocampista più di qualità e di quantità e la Juve una struttura difensiva più solida, però il vero problema è l’inaffidabilità. Ogni partita è impronosticabile».

#2217. Tare sul rapporto con Cardinale: "Non ebbi mai la possibilità di parlare più con lui"

Igli Tare, ex Direttore Sportivo del Milan, è stato protagonista dell’ultimo episodio di Sky Calcio Unplugged con Gianluca Di Marzio, Stefano Borghi e Fayna. Queste le sue dichiarazioni a 360° sull'esperienza in rossonero: dai colpi di mercato alla grande delusione di non andare in Champions, fino ad alcune dinamiche societarie e al rapporto con Gerry Cardinale. A proposito, questo un estratto delle sue parole sull'attuale proprietario americano di Redbird:

"Ricordo quando c’era la trattativa per Jashari… Ero appena atterrato a Roma e mi ha fatto molto piacere una sua telefonata perché voleva capire cosa stesse accadendo su quella trattativa. Gli ho spiegato tutte le dinamiche e mi è piaciuto molto che mi ha detto “Qualsiasi cosa di cui tu hai bisogno, se devi spendere qualche soldo in più fammi sapere perché io ci sono”. Poi durante quel percorso io non ho mai avuto la possibilità di parlare con lui, anche volutamente. Sopra di me c’erano altre persone che non ho mai voluto scavalcare. Non ho mai avuto un rapporto diretto con lui, e la possibilità di un confronto avrebbe aiutato tutti quanti. Non me, ma tutti quanti. Mettendo sul tavolo tutte le problematiche e le dinamiche potevamo risolvere le cose molto prima. Ma penso che per Cardinale sia un’esperienza nuova. Ha avuto esperienze negli altri sport in America. Ora ha fatto una cosa importante, prendendosi le responsabilità e mettendoci la faccia. Avrei preferito avere quella presenza anche quando c’ero io perché sarebbe stato molto utile. Ma per il Milan meglio tardi che mai. Ora lui nel bene e nel male prenderà le sue decisioni e responsabilità. Penso che anche per lui al primo posto c’è il bene del Milan”.

#2215. Declan Rice reveals he's stepped back from social media because it can 'ruin your whole day' after sick trolling of him and his girlfriend - as he poses in new photoshoot

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:36 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 08:45 EST, 9 November 2026

Declan Rice has opened up about reducing his use of social media - citing the mental toll it can have.

The Arsenal and England midfielder has been subjected to online abuse in the past - with his long-term partner Lauren Fryer having also been targeted.

Online abuse about her appearance had led to Fryer wiping all posts from her Instagram page back in 2024.

While Rice still has an Instagram account, he quit X three years ago as a result of the negativity that app can bring.

'I've not been back on the app since,' he told GQ Magazine - after being named among their Men of the Year. 'You could be having a great morning. You read one thing, and it just ruins your whole day.

'I feel like that's one of my strongest points... the ability to block out noise and not deal with that kind of stuff.'

Declan Rice has revealed he quit X three years ago due to the abuse he would receive online

Rice and long-term partner Lauren Fryer have been targeted in the past (pair pictured with their son Jude in May)

The midfielder says one post could 'ruin' his whole day - even if he was a great day beforehand

Rice, who has a four-year-old son called Jude with Fryer, is worried about the impact of social media on the younger generations.

'Screen time, for me, isn't a big thing,' he says of his own personal phone usage. 'I think social media for kids is 100 per cent a problem. I don't feel like there's as much personality now as there was a few years ago.'

As detailed by Daily Mail Sport last month, the 27-year-old is closing in on a new long-term deal at Arsenal believed to be worth around £350,000 per week.

The contract will put him on a level footing with Bukayo Saka at the top of the club's salary list.

And speaking about money in football as a whole, Rice told GQ Magazine that the finances within the sport are 'ridiculous' and despite his wealth he still wants to set a good example to his son Jude.

'The money that's in football as a whole is just ridiculous,' he continued. 'It's important to understand what things cost, even if you don't have to worry about paying for them.

'You still want to teach your kid values, not wanting them to be spoiled. You want them to work and to understand the value of life and money.

'It makes you more comfortable to be able to do things. But I don't wake up and think, "Oh, I've got loads of money", it's not the end goal.'

The 27-year-old is worried about the pitfalls of social media on the younger generations

The 27-year-old Arsenal and England star has been named in GQ Magazine's Men of the Year

Rice's focus will now be on his country with England hosting Croatia on Thursday night in the UEFA Nations League before travelling to World Cup champions Spain on Sunday.

Going into the November international break, the midfielder is enjoying a fine season with Arsenal who sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League with 27 points from their opening 10 matches.

#2214. “Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”: grande partecipazione al Maschio Angioino per l’iniziativa di Sinistra Italiana con Nicola Fratoianni

“Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”: grande partecipazione al Maschio Angioino per l’iniziativa di Sinistra Italiana con Nicola Fratoianni Napoli, 13 novembre 2026 – Si è tenuto ieri, giovedì 12 novembre, nella sala del Maschio Angioino a Napoli, l’incontro pubblico “Mezzogiorno, Napoli per l’alternativa”, promosso da Sinistra Italiana e Con il Lavoro. Un appuntamento centrale per delineare il futuro del Sud e avviare la costruzione di una proposta politica concreta, capace di rappresentare un’alternativa credibile alle politiche del Governo Meloni sul piano nazionale. All’evento, moderato dalla giornalista de La Repubblica Ilaria Urbani, hanno preso parte numerosi esponenti politici, istituzionali e della società civile: Nicola Fratoianni, Segretario Nazionale di Sinistra Italiana e Deputato per l’Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra; Peppe De Cristofaro, Capogruppo AVS al Senato; Pietro Rinaldi, Responsabile Enti Locali di Sinistra Italiana; Stefano Ioffredo, Segretario Provinciale della Federazione di Napoli di Sinistra Italiana; Toti Lange, Consigliere Comunale; Annalisa Senese, avvocata penalista; Daniele Cutolo, Presidente di Merqurio e avvocato. Hanno inoltre partecipato ai lavori il consigliere comunale Sergio D’Angelo, il co-portavoce regionale di Europa Verde Davide Secone e l’assessore Carlo Puca. Nel corso della riunione è stata ufficializzata un’importante novità organizzativa: l’attribuzione a Gianluca Daniele dell’incarico di coordinatore del Dipartimento Mezzogiorno di Sinistra Italiana, un passo strategico per radicare ulteriormente l’azione politica del partito sui temi dello sviluppo, del lavoro e della giustizia sociale nel Sud Italia. Di seguito gli estratti principali degli interventi. Gianluca Daniele (già Consigliere Regionale e neo-coordinatore del Dipartimento Mezzogiorno di Sinistra Italiana): “L’affetto di tanti amici e compagni ci fa capire che l’idea di questo percorso è importante per noi ma, soprattutto, per la nostra città. Il Mezzogiorno è ovviamente un tema principale per tutto il Paese, anche perché può essere la chiave per il campo progressista per provare a costruire una proposta alternativa vera. Le Elezioni nazionali si giocheranno qui al Sud, non solo per questioni di numeri ma per una questione politica. Il rapporto dello SVIMEZ riconosce l’impatto del PNRR sul Mezzogiorno, ma il dato più allarmante è che, dal 2021 al 2025, abbiamo perso 154 mila giovani che sono andati via. Se non c’è un lavoro stabile, se un laureato al Sud guadagna mille euro in meno rispetto a un laureato del Nord, è chiaro che ci sia la famosa ‘fuga dei cervelli’. Questo è il vero dramma del nostro Paese. Al Sud serve una politica pubblica vera: un progetto che metta le risorse ma, soprattutto, capace di mettere in moto l’economia. Le Elezioni politiche nel 2027 si vinceranno nel Mezzogiorno, bisogna dimostrare che il campo progressista possa realmente invertire questa tendenza. Questa sarebbe la vera scommessa: essere il Governo in grado di far ritornare le persone nel Mezzogiorno”. Toti Lange (Consigliere Comunale): “Vedere tanti ragazzi scendere in piazza è sicuramente una boccata di speranza. Noi, che facciamo una politica di territorio in una città come Napoli, siamo chiamati a confrontarci quotidianamente con i bisogni dei cittadini. Ci sono persone che vivono ogni giorno la disperazione. Dobbiamo costruire delle risposte. Napoli è la città che in pochi anni ha visto una crescita esponenziale della propria ricchezza in alcuni segmenti. La politica ha l’obbligo e il dovere di governare i processi. Non dobbiamo lasciare indietro le persone. Daremo il nostro contributo all’amministrazione Manfredi”. Peppe De Cristofaro (Capogruppo AVS al Senato): “Sono molto felice che sia partito questo percorso con Gianluca e Toti. Dobbiamo aprire le porte di AVS. Dobbiamo cercare di mettere nel governo delle città alcuni elementi di protagonismo. Questo Governo nazionale è stato nemico degli enti locali. Per creare una proposta reale alternativa alle destre, abbiamo l’occasione di creare un elemento di sinergia. Abbiamo l’esigenza di un programma che riduca le disuguaglianze”. Nicola Fratoianni (Segretario Nazionale di Sinistra Italiana e Deputato per l’Alleanza Verdi e Sinistra): “In questi quattro anni il Governo Meloni ha inventato 50 nuovi reati, 60 nuove aggravanti e quasi 500 anni di carcere in più. I giovani sono nemici dei governi di destra e i vari provvedimenti realizzati ne sono la dimostrazione. Questo Governo non dà più la dignità del lavoro ai giovani, che vanno all’estero. Si ha la folle pretesa di investire il 5% del PIL in spese militari per il contributo NATO. Dobbiamo consolidare una proposta politica che lavori per creare un’alleanza credibile per mandare a casa questa destra. I problemi sono reali e radicali e, dunque, richiedono una proposta politica che sappia dire redistribuzione e nuove politiche industriali. Bisogna saper dire che occorre investire nella sanità pubblica. Il ruolo del pubblico deve tornare a svolgere una funzione centrale. Dobbiamo andare nella direzione opposta alle politiche che creano disuguaglianze. La rassegnazione è il nostro grande avversario: dobbiamo dare forza ad AVS, portando più avanti gli obiettivi che, comunque, incominciamo a tratteggiare”. L’iniziativa del Maschio Angioino segna dunque l’avvio di una fase politica nuova per Napoli e per tutto il Sud: un laboratorio di idee e mobilitazione che pone la questione meridionale al centro dell’agenda progressista, con l’obiettivo dichiarato di costruire, a partire dai territori, una coalizione solida in grado di battere le destre e offrire al Paese una guida alternativa.

#2209. Endrick, tutti i numeri col Real Madrid: il Milan la vera occasione di rilancio?

Il talento di Endrick non può essere messo in discussione. Dribbling, velocità, abile con entrambi i piedi. Il brasiliano, nonostante la giovanissima età vanta già molta esperienza a livello internazionale. La maglia del Madrid è pesante e storica, proprio per questo tutto il suo potenziale, forse non è esploso del tutto. Con Ancelotti le difficoltà nel trovare spazio erano molte e anche con Mourinho le cose non sembrano essere cambiate. Il Milan potrebbe essere la vera occasione di rilancio per lui?

"Nonostante Mourinho continui a dire che Endrick resterà al Real Madrid, la verità è che in questo momento la palla ce l'ha il giocatore. Se il giocatore decide di comunicare al Real Madrid di voler provare una nuova esperienza per crescere e per giocare, il Real Madrid non si opporrà. E ti dico che le indicazioni sono proprio queste. Ad oggi non ci sono ancora state comunicazioni ufficiali tra le parti, ma ti confermo che Endrick, come ha dichiarato anche in una recente intervista, è aperto a una nuova esperienza in prestito stile Lione, che gli possa dare quel protagonismo e quel minutaggio in più anche in ottica nazionale. Endrick vuole giocare".

Il brasiliano con la maglia dei Blancos ha sin qui trovato poca fortuna ( e pochissimi minuti). In 47 presenze ufficiali, 8 reti e 2 assist. In questa stagione ha totalizzato finora 7 presenze condite da un gol in Champions contro la Roma e un assist.

#2208. Crisis-hit FIFA chief Gianni Infantino 'requested VIP treatment for his daughters and their dogs at Miami airport'

By DANIEL MATTHEWS, US SENIOR SPORTS WRITER

Published: 09:47 EST, 5 November 2026 | Updated: 12:07 EST, 9 November 2026

FIFA president Gianni Infantino is facing more uncomfortable questions after it emerged that his office asked for 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their pet dogs on a trip from Miami to Qatar.

Infantino's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months, with honorary Japanese FA president Kohzo Tashima announcing on Thursday that he will stand against Infantino in next year's presidential election.

On Thursday, The Times revealed that back in May, Infantino's presidential office wrote to Miami airport officials asking for someone to 'assist' three of his daughters - and their pets - through security for a personal trip to Qatar.

Miami airport's VIP protocol reportedly allows diplomats and other special guests to be escorted through security checkpoints up to the door of the plane. Officers can also request early boarding.

These privileges are not automatically laid on for loved ones traveling separately, with protocol stating that 'courtesies... will not be extended' to family members of VIPs 'when the families are traveling on their own.'

But according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail, members of Infantino's family enjoyed the airport's services dozens of times while traveling without the FIFA president between 2024 and 2026.

Gianni Infantino's office reportedly requested 'VIP treatment' for his daughters and their dogs

The FIFA president's future has been under the microscope after a scandal-laden few months

In a statement to The Times, Miami airport insisted these requests are dealt with 'on a case-by-case basis.' The Daily Mail has contacted FIFA for comment but a spokesperson told The Times: 'Port courtesy requests were made to Miami international airport (MIA), on the advice of a former adviser to the Fifa president.

'Port courtesies are provided at no charge to the president of Fifa given his position as the head of an association or NGO. Mr Infantino’s family members are also entitled to request these services under MIA’s own Courtesies of Port Handbook and these are also provided free of any charge, on a case-by-case basis, at the discretion of MIA.'

Infantino's position is already under threat heading into FIFA's presidential election next March, when he is hoping to be elected to a fourth term. Back in December, Infantino awarded Trump the inaugural FIFA Peace Prize – to widespread ridicule.

During the World Cup, the Balogun affair saw Infantino accused of favoritism and caving to the White House, while the FIFA president and Trump were mocked for handing over the trophy to Spain together.

Before long, Infantino faced a mutiny over his secret plans – later scrapped – to sell a stake in the World Cup to private equity investors including Joshua Kushner, the brother of Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

Then earlier this week, FIFA strongly denied allegations that Infantino influenced Trump administration officials to fast-track a work permit for his undocumented Nicaraguan housekeeper after she lost her legal status, according to bombshell documents.

The global soccer chief is alleged to have turned to politically-connected contacts to secure a new work permit for Yajarlin del Socorro Fernandez after the White House revoked her legal permission to work in the United States, according to documents reviewed by the Daily Mail.

#2203. Tresoldi lascia la Germania Under 21: niente Belgio dopo il trauma cranico

Lo staff medico ha fermato per precauzione anche Hendry Blank e ha autorizzato entrambi a tornare ai rispettivi club.

Nicolò Tresoldi salterà la sfida della Germania Under 21 contro il Belgio e tornerà al Bruges dopo aver riportato un trauma cranico in nazionale. Secondo quanto riportato da SportMediaset, L’attaccante si è scontrato testa contro testa con il compagno Hendry Blank durante la rifinitura.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il contatto è avvenuto in un contrasto aereo. Il ct Antonio Di Salvo ha confermato l’episodio alla vigilia della partita con il Belgio: Tresoldi, che nell’azione era riuscito a segnare, ha accusato mal di testa dopo l’impatto. Blank ha invece riportato una commozione cerebrale.

Le condizioni dei due giocatori non destano particolari preoccupazioni. Lo staff medico ha comunque disposto uno stop precauzionale per gestire le conseguenze dello scontro: entrambi sono stati esclusi dalla gara e autorizzati a rientrare nei rispettivi club. SportMediaset riferisce che Tresoldi lascerà così il ritiro della nazionale giovanile tedesca.

#2201. Wayne Rooney and Paddy McGuinness laud football super-agent Paul Stretford - who has worked with Man United icon since his teens - at star-studded Global Football Industry Awards

Published: 13:14 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:15 EST, 9 November 2026

Wayne Rooney has led the praise for football super-agent Paul Stretford as the industry heavyweight was honoured at the Global Football Industry Awards.

Stretford, alongside Kenneth Shepherd, received the prestigious Lifetime Achievement Award at this year's Awards in recognition of their longstanding careers and work on Soccer Aid for Unicef.

He has worked by Rooney's side for more than 20 years, and has recently appeared on the former footballer's reality TV show, which he fronts alongside wife Coleen.

Rooney presented Stretford with the award himself, alongside Toni Duggan and comedian Paddy McGuinness. Theo Walcott and Jamie Carragher hosted the ceremony.

Rooney said of his agent and close friend: 'Paul in particular has had a major influence on my life since I was a teenager and has guided my career.

'Both Paul and Kenneth are very deserving of this award. It is not before time and I'm delighted for both of them. The work they've done on Soccer Aid is phenomenal too.'

Wayne Rooney (centre) has lauded close friend and football super agent Paul Stretford (right)

Stretford doesn't just look after Rooney, having also worked with the likes of Harry Maguire since founding Proactive Sports Management, now known as Triple S Sports Group, in 1987.

Shepherd, meanwhile, has been instrumental in the success of the Soccer Aid initiative which has raised more than £137million for Unicef since it launched in 2006.

McGuinness added: 'I'm so proud to pay tribute to a duo who have had a profound impact on football and two figures we've both had the pleasure of working with over the years. Together, they built the Triple S Group into a dynamic force in British and international football.'

England assistant manager Anthony Barry also carried out an exclusive Q&A at the event, which saw Tyler Alexander-Arnold, brother of England defender Trent, also scoop a top award.

The brother of the Real Madrid star represents Jordan Henderson, Jarrod Bowen and Andy Robertson as well as his sibling, who saw his PLG Agency bought by Gersh talent agency in May of this year.

L'Inter cerca davvero una quinta punta? A rispondere è Riccardo Trevisani che, intervistato da Radio Mana Mana Sport, ha fatto un nome in grado di esaltare i tifosi nerazzurri. Quello di Endrick del Real Madrid.

Ecco le sue parole: "Ricordatevi sempre che Endrick non è una passione solo della Roma: è un giocatore che piace anche sotto al Duomo e interessa a Inter e Milan. Non sarà facile prima di tutto toglierlo al Real Madrid e poi portarlo alla Roma eventualmente.

Se l'Inter cerca altri attaccanti? Tieni presente che Lautaro sta fuori da un mese e ancora non è fissato il rientro, Thuram salta 2-3 mesi ogni stagione, Bonny è un po' sotto il livello dei primi tre: se possono implementare, implementano".

#2197. A failed spell at Wolves almost saw him walk away from football ...now Danny Armstrong is idolised in Romania as he attempts to lead Dinamo Bucharest back to former glories

Published: 13:42 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 13:52 EST, 9 November 2026

The daughter says: ‘Da’. Darby Armstrong, all of two years old, is not calling out for her father, Danny.

‘She is saying “Yes” in Romanian. She can count to ten in Romanian,’ says her proud father. She may have to learn to count higher, and quickly, to chart her father’s figures in the Superliga with Dinamo Bucharest.

Armstrong sits in an upmarket restaurant in the beautiful suburbs of Bucharest with a park stretching towards a lake. He sips ginger tea with honey and engages with waiters, diners and children who approach him for a chat and a photograph.

‘Darby is a bit bemused by it,’ he says. ‘We were in the mall there and a guy wanted a pic. I could see her looking up to see what all the fuss was about.’

Armstrong could be forgiven for being ever so slightly bemused himself. At 29, he has taken a few dunts and not just from enthusiastic full-backs. Success has hardly been overnight.

‘I nearly gave up once,’ he says quietly. ‘Another time I thought it was all over and I was looking at one-to-one coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Danny Armstrong is hailed after his match-winning heroics in a crucial win over UTA Arad

He survived, though. He is a hero at Dinamo. There is a clamour on matchday when he comes out of the tunnel. The ultras, high behind a goal, chant his name with a fervour that suddenly breaks out in red flares and manic jumping.

It is a long way from Ayr. Armstrong knows he did not walk it alone. His saviours include John McGlynn, who brought him to Raith Rovers, George Cairns, who convinced him to stay at Hamilton, and Scott Sellars, the youth coach who advised him to leave Wolverhampton Wanderers for first team football.

He also took inspiration from many team-mates, including Kieran Tierney who was once his room-mate in a Scotland under-age team,

‘I was meant to be rooming with another left-back but he pulled out and this young player from Celtic came in,’ recalls Armstrong. ‘He wasn’t even in the squad initially and now he is Scotland’s best left-back alongside Robbo.

‘I used to play against KT so many times and I have great respect for him, playing so many games for Celtic, getting that move to Arsenal and coming back to Scotland to win trophies. The setbacks he has had… he’s an inspiration.

‘He has resilience. He has motivation. He took the half opportunity that was offered to him and ran with it.’

Armstrong has done the same in Bucharest. He has been bolstered by his past. ‘It builds you,’ he says of his experience. ‘There have been tough spells but you can look back and make sense of them and see how they have helped you. Football takes a lot of work.’

Armstrong has thrived in Romania since making the leftfield switch to Dinamo Bucharest

It takes a lot of belief too. That can be a capricious quality, seemingly dependent on the winds of fortune.

Armstrong can point to two hat-tricks that gave him faith in a time of need. ‘I scored a hat-trick for Hamilton in a youth game at Auchenhowie against Rangers,’ he says. ‘That came after I had been convinced to stick at it.’

He also scored three last season in the derby against Steaua. ‘That was crazy,’ he says. ‘I don’t think I have realised even yet how big it was. People tell me it was the greatest day in their lives. We hadn’t beaten them in five or six years. We were also in a bad spot with poor form. And then I score three. It gives me goosebumps even now.’

He adds: ‘There is a real football culture here. It means so much to people and I love that. It actually wasn’t too hard to come here because I had looked at it a year earlier but stayed on at Kilmarnock. When Dinamo came in and showed me videos and talked about the history, I was on board.’

There was one decisive factor. ‘I knew it was time to try to make a name for myself somewhere else. I wanted to test myself, keep myself open to other opportunities, try to get to the highest level I can get.’

He is professionally coy about the prospect of international football, having again missed out on Sebastien Pocognoli’s latest Scotland squad. He maintains the line of concentrating on his club form, having a dream to play for his country, and hoping to be noticed.

Armstrong was a big hit at Kilmarnock and has long been mooted for a Scotland call-up

His performances in Romania, though, have been so outstanding that there may be the odd glance from the Pocognoli camp at just what is happening at Dinamo. They may have to be quick as Armstrong qualifies for Ireland too.

He plays in a wide right role, with the freedom to cut inside and become a playmaker. His manager, Nuno Campos, has faith in him. He is the latest in a line of characters who have led him from doubt to conviction.

There is no hesitation. ‘It was McGlynn who saved me,’ says Armstrong. But there were previous tribulations that required the intervention of football folk and Armstrong is immensely grateful.

‘I had been going up to Hamilton from Ayr every night as a kid, playing at the weekend, and by the time I was about 15 I think I was drained. I felt I was missing out on other things in life. It was tough on my parents, too, who did everything for me. The family always sacrificed themselves for me.’

His parents told George Cairns, Hamilton coach, that their son did not want to continue. The reply was instant: ‘Get him up here and I will have a chat with him.’

The crisis passed after this talk and that hat-trick against Rangers. But further tribulations were to come.

Armstrong's relentless drive and enthusiasm have made him a standout player in Romania

Armstrong headed to Wolverhampton Wanderers, spurning an offer by Rangers under Mark Warburton and Davie Weir. ‘That was a mistake,’ he says. He was never near first team football at Wolves though the club wanted to retain him. After a chat with Scott Sellars, he took the chance to leave and start again.

‘That was very, very difficult,’ he says. ‘I did not play from May to November. I was sitting by the phone, urging it to ring with an offer. I had thoughts about packing it all in and going into coaching or being a personal trainer.’

Then an unlikely Superman came to the rescue in the shape of McGlynn, then Raith manager. ‘That changed everything, everything,’ says Armstrong.

A bounce game was organised to assess the player but Armstrong admits the team’s performance was awful. ‘I was very much part of that,’ he says.

He did much better in another friendly but budget considerations meant McGlynn could offer only a nine-game contract. ‘It was a couple of hundred quid a week but it meant everything to me.’ Five goals in nine games led to an extended contract.

‘He is a genius,’ says Armstrong. ‘He is so big on detail, detail, detail. He is a fantastic football coach. It’s an obsession for him.

‘I have never met a man like him. He saved my football career and made me believe I could make it.’

John McGlynn helped save Armstrong's career by taking him under his wing at Raith Rovers

After a spell at Ross County, Armstrong flourished under Derek McInnes at Kilmarnock and the move to Romania offered further scope for growth.

‘It was a bit difficult at first settling in but now my partner, Lauren, and Darby love it. We have made friends,’ he says.

At this a couple of waiters approach the table with grins and cheery banter. Armstrong responds with a warm handshake and that half-embrace that signals another acquiescence to yet another picture.

‘The big difference this season is the coach,’ says Armstrong. ‘He has come in and completely changed the environment and the atmosphere. He has brought fun back and he makes you want to come into training.’

Dinamo are now sitting joint-top of the league. ‘The first goal has to be European football, getting this club back to where it belongs,’ he says.

Armstrong has his sights set on an historic Romanian title and is not ruling out a longer stay

The Dinamo fans, who have not witnessed a league title in 20 years, sense Superliga glory. ‘We are a good side and we play nice stuff,’ says Armstrong. ‘But let’s take it game by game.’

He has the same laid-back attitude to his contract. ‘It expires at the end of the season and there is an option there but we leave all that to after Christmas.’

He is happy in Bucharest but knows the fate of a footballer is never predictable. ‘It is a wonderful place. The fans are great and the manager has faith in me.’

He points out that Campos wants him to be a ‘monster’. This is an instruction to be powerful and innovative in the final third.

The next night Armstrong swivels just outside the box and hits a wonderful shot to open the scoring against UTA Arad.

He then sprints towards the stand where Lauren and Darby are celebrating. He has just been a monster. But he is still a dad, in whatever language.

Martedì 17 novembre, dalle ore 12:00 fino a mezzanotte.
