#2126. Lazio, Gattuso chiede di più per lo staff. Frattesi: «mi ha salvato la vita»

Dopo il gol in Italia-Francia, il centrocampista racconta quanto siano stati importanti giocare e sentire fiducia.

La Lazio vuole prolungare il contratto di Gennaro Gattuso fino al 2029, ma il tecnico prende tempo e pone una richiesta nella trattativa: un aumento per il suo staff di nove persone. Prima di decidere, vuole anche capire che cosa accadrà nel mercato di gennaio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Alla pausa per le nazionali di novembre, i biancocelesti sono primi da soli in Serie A con 29 punti. Hanno la miglior difesa e il terzo miglior attacco del campionato. La squadra gioca con forza e aggressività, coinvolgendo tutti gli undici uomini sia nella fase difensiva sia in quella offensiva.

Gattuso ha dato alla formazione un’identità riconoscibile. che riprende quanto riportato dal Messaggero, la dirigenza si è già messa al lavoro per trovare un accordo con l’allenatore. Il suo rendimento sta attirando anche l’interesse di diverse squadre europee.

Il contratto attuale lega Gattuso alla Lazio fino al 2027 per 1,2 milioni di euro. È prevista un’opzione di rinnovo fino al 2028 collegata al dodicesimo posto, ma il club sta trattando una scadenza più lontana. Il percorso della squadra arriva nonostante le difficoltà economiche della società e le contestazioni dei tifosi nei confronti del presidente Claudio Lotito.

Gattuso, per ora, non ha dato una risposta. Vuole vedere se a gennaio resteranno le limitazioni che in estate hanno condizionato gli acquisti della Lazio e se la società dovrà effettuare cessioni. Lotito gli ha promesso che nella sessione invernale non ci saranno partenze, ma l’allenatore attende gli sviluppi del mercato.

Nella trattativa c’è poi la questione dello staff. I nove collaboratori guadagnano attualmente circa 700mila euro complessivi, poco più di 77mila euro a testa in media. Per Gattuso la cifra non riconosce adeguatamente il lavoro svolto negli allenamenti e i risultati ottenuti in campo.

#2124. QPR must take January action over 24-year-old who has not made a league appearance since August: Opinion

QPR refined their squad with a handful of incomings and outgoings in the summer transfer window. It has yielded good results at Loftus Road, but some of those who headed out the exit door have not found the fortunes they would have hoped for.

Among those in that category is goalkeeper Joe Walsh. The 24-year-old saw a loan move away from West London sanctioned, with Pierce Charles becoming the new No. 1 while on loan from Manchester City and new signing Calum Ward locking down the spot as his backup.

Walsh was sent to League One with Wigan Athletic, but things have unravelled fairly quickly for him in the North West. And, having lost his starting berth, QPR should be recalling him when the winter transfer window comes around.

Walsh took the No. 1 shirt upon arrival at Wigan Athletic and looked poised to be their starting ‘keeper. However, a tough start to the season saw the Latics lose their first three League One games while conceding six goals in the process, and they were knocked out of the Carabao Cup too.

Then, just before the end of the transfer window, Joe Whitworth was signed from Crystal Palace. The 22-year-old has since locked down the place as Gary Caldwell‘s starting shot-stopper, leaving Walsh to watch on from the bench in every league match since.

The difference in their stats is rather glaring. It must be noted that Walsh’s numbers are from a smaller sample size, but he recorded a save rate of just 40% compared to Whitworth’s 69.8%, and the QPR loanee’s xG prevented sits at -2.03 compared to Whitworth’s impressive +4.45 (all stats via FotMob).

In truth, Whitworth’s importance in goal means it feels unlikely that Walsh will reclaim his place. He has started in the EFL Trophy games – all of which have ended in victory – but the Hoops man was on the bench for the FA Cup clash at Boreham Wood.

The purpose of Walsh’s loan move away from QPR was to find game time. However, evidence shows he is not finding the opportunities needed.

He did not play for the Hoops before joining the Latics, so would not be restricted by the two-club rule. As such, the Championship side should look to send the goalkeeper out again.

A drop to League Two could offer Walsh the starting berth he desires. Opportunities in Scotland could also prove fruitful as he bids to find the game time he needs to develop.

#2123. Rio Ferdinand claps back at fans mocking him for celebrating Man United's late equaliser against Aston Villa which left them in the relegation zone

Published: 14:15 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:16 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at football fans who criticised his reaction on social media to Manchester United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Former United defender Ferdinand drew criticism when he shared a photo of himself celebrating after the Red Devils' dramatic comeback on Sunday afternoon.

Michael Carrick's side had looked down and out at 4-2 in stoppage time, but late strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu meant they earned a point from the game.

They did, though, remain in the relegation zone – however Ferdinand shared two snaps to his X account following full-time.

The first showed the 48-year-old with his head in his hands, and the second saw him celebrating. He captioned the post: 'From this to THIS!!! Carrick time!!!!!!!!!! Birthday weekend just got (a) tad better in the last 6 minutes…'

Fans though flooded the replies with criticism, questioning why he was 'celebrating a draw' and calling him an 'embarrassment'. Ferdinand, though, has now taken the opportunity to respond.

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at fans who criticised his response to Manchester United's draw with Aston Villa

'Let me just address something,' Ferdinand began on Rio Ferdinand Presents. 'On socials I put a picture up and little comment underneath of me going like that (celebrates).

'That's not me celebrating a point against Aston Villa, by the way, it's me celebrating a moment in a football match. It's what football does to you. It can take over your body, take over your emotions in a moment. That moment isn't the big picture.

'So all of these people saying his standards have dropped and he's celebrating a draw... I'm not celebrating a draw against Villa, I'm celebrating the moment and the fact we actually came back and showed a bit of character.

'It's always about that moment that when you calm down and you go, look where we are in the league, that's terrible, looks how things unfolded in the game, that needs work. But, in the moment, as a football fan, you are allowed to get carried away with it.

'That's what football does. If you don't know that or don't understand it or feel it, you're not a football person, so get out.'

Ferdinand hasn't shied away from criticising his former team-mate Carrick amid United's poor run of form that has left them in 18th in the Premier League table.

United came back from behind to draw 4-4 with Villa having looked down and out in the game

His assessment of Sunday's showing was more tame, with the ex-centre back describing the effort as full of both character and chaos.

He added: 'It's like we need a punch on the nose, or two or three, to start playing. But then, the flip side of it, it's character and ability plays a part in that.

'In the end, we could have won it. But they are giving us fans grey hairs. It's crazy football.'

As thrilling as Man United's fight-back may have been to some fans, manager Carrick was still forced to answer difficult questions at full-time.

Sky Sports' Patrick Davison asked the former captain what he 'expected to happen over the next few weeks' - suggesting a question mark still lingering over his tenure despite comebacks against Roma and Villa.

Carrick's response was understandably thorny, with the manager underlining that he 'probably' would not be walking away from the role.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week.

#2122. Sebastiano Esposito, l’agente: “Ora non pensa al mercato, ma potrebbe giocare benissimo in un tridente con Hojlund e Vergara”

A Radio Napoli Centrale, nel corso di Un Calcio alla Radio, è intervenuto l’agente Mario Giuffredi: “Io vivo le partite dei miei assistiti con grande passione e coinvolgimento. Come se fossi con loro in campo. Durante la partita non riesco a essere distaccato, sono molto acceso. Dopo la partita, ritorna l’equilibrio. E riesco anche a essere più equilibrato delle critiche degli stessi calciatori. Come ho vissuto i due rigori degli Esposito? Non ho visto nessuno dei due rigori di Pio e Sebastiano. Ero anche a cena con Salvatore Esposito. Capivamo in base alle reazioni degli altri che erano con noi a tavola. Pio sentiva la responsabilità della partita. Aver segnato quel rigore contro la Francia toglieva il pensiero del rigore della Bosnia. Pio ha una lunga carriera, può migliorare statistiche con Nazionale e club. Io non guardo le pagelle, so come ragionano i giornalisti, che non si limitano a guardare la prestazione, ma anche episodi, dettagli. La prestazione di Sebastiano è stata saggia a livello tattico. Ha giocato in posizioni di campo non suoi. Mi dispiace che i giornalisti non si limitano a questo, ma si limitano a guardare il rigore sbagliato. Per sbagliare quel rigore, devi avere il coraggio di batterlo. Sull’1-1, contro quel portiere (Maignan ndr) e contro quella Nazionale, devi avere coraggio. Io mi ero arrabbiato con Sebastiano se non avesse avuto il coraggio di andare dal disco. Sebastiano Esposito e Vergara insieme con Hojlund? Si incastrerebbero benissimo, perché Sebastiano è un toro a livello fisico. Vergara ha grande forza nelle gambe. Hanno anche colpi tecnici, sono imprevedibili. Non sarebbe maschio. Però non facciamo i direttori del Napoli né gli allenatori del Napoli. Aiutare il Napoli portando Sebastiano Esposito? Io non mi sono mai sottratto ad aiutare il Napoli e mai lo farò. Al tempo stesso non sono io che vado a insistere per far prendere quel tipo di giocatore. Sono orgoglioso di quello che sono. Il fatto di essere arrivato dalla galetta mi rende orgoglioso. Negli ultimi due anni ho avuto la media di quattro giocatori convocati in Nazionale. Vedo che nel primo e nel secondo tempo ho due giocatori su tre in campo. Ieri sera dopo la partita, presa coscienza, ho preso l’auto e sono andato nei luoghi dove tutto è iniziato. Per un napoletano è tutto più difficile, ci sono tantissimi ostacoli messi davanti da invidiosi. Hai sentito Pio Esposito dopo la partita contro la Francia? Il futuro di Pio è all’Inter, senza dubbio. Sta benissimo. Il club ha mostrato sempre attacco e riconoscenza. Sebastiano si trova benissimo al Sassuolo, in questo momento non pensare neanche al mercato. Quello che succederà si vedrà. Entrambi stanno bene dove stanno. Pio sicuramente rimarrà all’Inter per tanti anni, è la sua seconda pelle; mentre Sebastiano magari si vedrà strada facendo se sia meritevole di alzare ancora di più il livello, ma è prematuro parlare di mercato.Il paragone di Pio Esposito con Meazza? Noi vediamo tutto con serenità ed equilibrio. Io vivo con questa concezione: ci addormentiamo la sera con la consapevolezza che il mattino possa finire tutto. Questo ci permette di non cullarci su certe cose. Il calcio è lo sport più bello e più crudo del mondo. Uno dei più grandi giocatori per me è stato Roberto Baggio. Lui a tratti viene dimenticato, nessuno gli ha dato un posto di un certo livello. Il calcio ha bisogno di gente come Roberto Baggio. Questo mi fa pensare che un giocatore verrà dimenticato in un secondo. Perciò bisogna vivere tutto con equilibrio. Qual è il prossimo che la mia scuderia ha in rampa di lancio? Te ne dico due. Quando dico le cose ci metto la faccia e vado anche controcorrente. Dico Favasuli e Marianucci. Per me Marianucci può arrivare in Nazionale, è un difensore di grandissimo livello. Ha qualcosa in più rispetto a tanti altri. Se migliora nell’attenzione, diventa di grande livello. Favasuli lo diamo per scontato, perché è partito bene”.

#2120. Corea del Sud, ancora tensioni nello spogliatoio: Son e altri quattro big negano l’addio

La Corea del Sud vive giorni delicati dopo le indiscrezioni su una presunta spaccatura tra alcuni dei suoi principali giocatori. Le voci di tensioni nello spogliatoio hanno portato cinque elementi di riferimento della Nazionale a pubblicare un comunicato congiunto per fare chiarezza e smentire l’ipotesi di un possibile abbandono della selezione per chiedere cambiamenti.

Al centro della discussione ci sarebbe stato un confronto generazionale tra il capitano Son Heung-min, attaccante dei Los Angeles FC, Lee Jae-sung e il gruppo formato dai giocatori classe 1996, tra cui Kim Min-jae del Bayern Monaco, Hwang In-beom e Hwang Hee-chan. Le divergenze sarebbero emerse dopo il pareggio contro il Venezuela e la vittoria sull’Uzbekistan dello scorso ottobre, quando alcuni calciatori avevano espresso dubbi sul rendimento della squadra.

Durante il ritiro in Qatar, i cinque protagonisti hanno incontrato la stampa attraverso un comunicato diffuso dalla Federazione coreana. "Le discussioni non sono nate da conflitti personali con un giocatore specifico, ma da una preoccupazione comune sulla necessità che la Nazionale migliori", hanno spiegato. I calciatori hanno inoltre negato di aver mai minacciato di lasciare la selezione per ottenere determinate condizioni: "È completamente falso che abbiamo cercato di imporre richieste in cambio del nostro ritiro".

La situazione arriva in un periodo già difficile per il calcio sudcoreano, reduce dall’eliminazione nella fase a gironi del Mondiale 2026 e dal successivo addio del commissario tecnico Hong Myung-bo. Attualmente la squadra è guidata ad interim dallo spagnolo Roberto Moreno, che ha comunque convocato tutti i giocatori coinvolti nella vicenda. Nel primo match dopo l’esplosione del caso, però, la Corea del Sud è stata battuta 3-2 dall’Arabia Saudita in amichevole disputata in Qatar. Il prossimo impegno sarà contro il Qatar il 17 novembre.

#2119. Blackburn Rovers confirm extent of Ryan Alebiosu injury blow with return timeline set

Blackburn Rovers have seen Ryan Alebiosu become a key player since his signing in the summer of 2025. He was their Player of the Season in the 2025/26 campaign and has retained his starting berth under Tony Mowbray this term too.

However, Alebiosu was forced off in the first half of the 2-1 defeat to Stoke City at the start of the month and missed the win over West Ham as a result. Now, Rovers have confirmed the 24-year-old has undergone surgery on his knee and will be sidelined until 2027.

Alebiosu will now work through a rehabilitation programme with the Rovers medical staff in the hope that he can recover swiftly and get back to action over the second half of the campaign.

Alebiosu is ideal as a wing-back or attack-minded full-back. He’s got the athleticism to deal with the demands of getting up and down the right-hand side, and the energy to recover and see to his defensive duties.

He offers great assets in both thirds too, recording six assists across his Blackburn Rovers career to date. The former Arsenal youngster is a great tackler too, anticipating his opponent’s movements well and showing patience and timing to nick the ball.

He’s a big asset on the right for Rovers when attacking and defending, and his presence will be missed. The hope is that surgery reduces the risk of Alebiosu suffering a worse issue further down the line.

Losing Alebiosu is a blow, but one man who will relish the chance to impress is Gady Beyuku. Signed from Modena FC in the summer, the 20-year-old had only made four substitute appearances for Blackburn Rovers before his fellow right-back was cast to the sidelines.

The Frenchman will be determined to prove he’s up to the task of Championship football, as he is the only other natural right-back on the books. It marks a big chance for Beyuku to earn his place in Mowbray’s side.

Youngster Matty Litherland is working his way back to fitness and could come into consideration. Kristi Montgomery has covered on the right as well, but he has progressed well in central midfield, and it would be a blow to break up his partnership with Sam Morsy.

Opportunity knocks for Beyuku while Alebiosu recovers, so it will be intriguing to see just how he fares.

#2118. Napoli, occhi sempre su Zirkzee: duello con la Juve per Varela. Il punto di Mediaset

Negli ultimi giorni sono molti i nomi che sono finiti sul taccuino del ds Giovanni Manna. L’ultimo, quello di Joshua Zirkzee. Il Napoli continua a lavorare sul mercato alla ricerca di un rinforzo offensivo da affiancare a Hojlund. Il più seguito è Varela, ma arrivare al centravanti del Monza già a gennaio non sarà semplice. Le sue nove reti, che ne fanno il capocannoniere della Serie A, saranno fondamentali nella corsa salvezza della squadra di Juric. Privarsi del proprio attaccante più prolifico a metà stagione rappresenterebbe un sacrificio importante per il club brianzolo. Una difficoltà che spinge Manna a guardarsi intorno e a valutare anche soluzioni alternative.

Su Varela, intanto, si registra anche l’interesse della Juventus, dando vita a un possibile derby di mercato tra bianconeri e azzurri. Il Napoli segue e apprezza il 21enne portoghese: nelle scorse ore il club ha raccolto informazioni attraverso il suo entourage, approfondendo anche gli aspetti economici dell’operazione. La concorrenza e soprattutto il peso del giocatore negli equilibri del Monza rendono però la trattativa particolarmente complicata.

Ecco perché Manna sta battendo anche altre piste, con uno sguardo rivolto soprattutto alla Premier League, dove non mancano occasioni da cogliere. Una porta a Joshua Zirkzee, 25 anni, attualmente al Manchester United. L’olandese conosce bene la Serie A, dove si era messo in mostra nella stagione 2023/24 con la maglia del Bologna. Sotto la guida di Thiago Motta aveva realizzato 11 gol e 5 assist, contribuendo alla storica qualificazione dei rossoblù in Champions League. Numeri e prestazioni che avevano convinto lo United a investire 42,5 milioni di euro per portarlo a Old Trafford.

A Manchester, però, il percorso dell’attaccante ha subito una battuta d’arresto. In questa stagione ha trovato poco spazio, collezionando appena 186 minuti e due reti in dieci partite. Una situazione che potrebbe favorire un’eventuale partenza e trasformare l’olandese in un’opportunità nel mercato di gennaio. Il Napoli osserva e vuole provarci: l’olandese potrebbe rappresentare una soluzione per completare il reparto e offrire a Hojlund un compagno e ad Allegri un’alternativa con caratteristiche diverse rispetto all’attaccante danese.

Per arrivare a Zirkzee, però, il Napoli dovrà prima fare i conti anche con il mercato in uscita. Le posizioni di Lang e Lucca sono quelle da monitorare con maggiore attenzione: entrambi potrebbero lasciare spazio a nuovi innesti e diventare le prime pedine sacrificabili per fare cassa. Eventuali cessioni permetterebbero a Manna di recuperare risorse da reinvestire sul mercato e provare a dare concretezza all’ipotesi che porta all’attaccante dello United. La strada per Zirkzee passa dunque anche dalle uscite: il Napoli valuta le occasioni in entrata, ma prima dovrà trovare le condizioni economiche per affondare il colpo.

#2117. Tare: “Senza il Covid penso avremmo vinto quello Scudetto. Lotito e Inzaghi…”

Ai microfoni del podcast Sky Calcio Unplugged condotto da Gianluca Di Marzio è stato intervistato l’ex diesse della Lazio, Igli Tare

Ai microfoni del podcast Sky Calcio Unplugged condotto da Gianluca Di Marzio è stato intervistato l’ex diesse della Lazio, Igli Tare.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Sono felice per la Lazio di oggi. La società ha creato una squadra competitiva e ha scelto Gattuso, che ha creato un clima positivo: tutti gli vogliono bene. Questa è una società con grande storia, rimarrò sempre legato alla Lazio. Ho un legame forte con questo club.

Abbiamo avuto degli approcci ma era più un'idea di Lotito. Conosco Rino, ho un rapporto molto bello con lui. Sono molto contento per lui.

Penso di sì. Era una storia molto bella. Prima della pandemia eravamo devastanti, dopo 20' eravamo già 2-0 o 3-0 per noi". Una chiacchiera significativa con Inzaghi, al tempo allenatore della Lazio: "All'inizio della stagione parlai con Simone e mi disse: ‘Igli, sei preoccupato?’. E io: ‘Io per niente, sono straconvinto che lotteremo per vincere lo Scudetto’. E lui: ‘Ma tu sei matto’. E io: ‘Fidati che sarà un'annata particolare ma molto bella per noi.

Penso che Ciro sia un ragazzo unico. Molto sensibile, aveva bisogno dell'ambiente che gli dava fiducia. E poi è stato straordinario, ha scritto la storia della Lazio. Un giocatore irripetibile.

Parliamo di un centroavanti fenomenale per il modo di interpretare il gioco e nella Lazio, per vari motivi, non ha dato quello che poteva dare. Aveva un aereo privato con destinazione Parigi al PSG. Ma lui ha rifiutato per venire alla Lazio. Ha rifiutato anche più del doppio di stipendio che gli è stato proposto da altre parti per venire in Italia.

Lui aveva l'ambizione di giocare il Mondiale 2014 e all’epoca nessun club gli dava un contratto con più di un anno. C'erano Galatasaray, Valencia, ma sempre per un anno. Io gli ho dato un contratto di tre anni, ho convinto anche Lotito. Quando abbiamo firmato tutti mi hanno massacrato perché stavamo pagando uno di 32 anni che aveva vissuto un anno negativo con qualche infortunio. Ma dopo il primo/secondo allenamento tutti hanno capito che era un fuoriclasse.

Con lui ho un legame molto speciale, abbiamo giocato insieme. Ha intrapreso una carriera che per tanti era una sorpresa ma per me mai. La reputo una persona molto curiosa, intelligente nella gestione. Poi è cresciuto tanto con l’esperienza alla Lazio e all'Inter. Quando tornerà, non so se in Italia o all’estero, penso che sarà un allenatore completo. L'esperienza più bella che ho vissuto? Con Delio Rossi. Ero giocatore con lui per tre annie quando Lotito gli comunicò che io sarei stato il nuovo DS lui rimase sorpreso e disse 'allora mi vuoi mandare via?’. Cambiare da giocatore a diventare "il capo di un allenatore" era una sorpresa anche per me, non mi aspettavo questa scelta di Lotito.

#2116. Gabbia sulla discontinuità del Milan: "Ha detto bene Amorim, serve crescere nell'approccio"

Matteo Gabbia questo venerdì ha visitato la scuola secondaria "Toscanini" di Milano in una bella giornata organizzata da Fondazione Milan. Di seguito le parole del centrale rossonero, attualmente infortunato sulla stagione dei rossoneri, con gli alti del campionato alternati finora ai bassi dell'Europa League.

Sul rientro dall'infortunio: "A gennaio potrei tornare ad allenarmi in gruppo, potrebbe essere quello il periodo. Stiamo cercando di lavorare molto e fare tutto nel miglior modo possibile. Ringrazio i fisioterapisti, non voglio che l'infortunio ricapiti ed è giusto prendermi il tempo corretto per tornare quando starò bene. Finora è stata una stagione sfortunata per me".

Sugli alti e bassi del Milan: "Dobbiamo cercare di capire l'importanza di ogni gara. L'altro giorno mister Amorim ha detto una cosa importante sul non vincere. Dobbiamo approcciare nel miglior modo possibile ogni partita. Vedo però un gruppo sano, e con tanta voglia di lavorare. Sono sicuro che abbiamo tutto il tempo per migliorare e fare un anno importante".

#2115. Man United's new boss contenders: Mauricio Pochettino tops the bookies' favourites ahead of Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann on 14-man list of top candidates

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:12 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 05:18 EST, 10 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookies' leading candidate to replace under-fire Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach should the latter get sacked.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport late on Monday night, Carrick is facing the sack during this November international break as a result of United's disastrous season so far.

Scrutiny on his role has intensified with the Red Devils now in the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

And Betfair have the Argentine as the favourite to succeed Carrick should he be dismissed within the next fortnight before United travel to bitter rivals Liverpool on November 22.

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookmakers' favourite to become the next Man United head coach

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is expected to get the sack after a poor start

As of 8.12am on Tuesday morning, they have him at 4/7 with out of work trio Eddie Howe (5/2), Julian Nagelsmann (5/1) and Didier Deschamps (15/2) the next favourites.

Antonio Conte and Aston Villa manager Unai Emery (both 9/1) follow the aforementioned quartet in the odds.

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler, Kieran McKenna, who worked with Carrick as an assistant manager to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and ex-England manager Gareth Southgate are all 20/1.

Southgate's successor Thomas Tuchel is 28/1 alongside Diego Simeone, Sebastian Hoeness and Cesc Fabregas.

Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner is 33/1 too.

As Daily Mail Sport detailed, although it's understood that no final decision has been reached over Carrick's future and insiders say that speculation over his sacking is premature, the expectation within Old Trafford is that a new man will be in charge for the visit to Anfield a week on Sunday.

Carrick replaced Ruben Amorim in mid-January and the former United midfielder was handed a two-year contract in May after guiding United to a third-place finish and qualification for the Champions League, losing just two of his 17 games as head coach.

However, he has only won three of 15 games in all competitions. Breaking it down even further, the 45-year-old has overseen United's worst top-flight start since Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago - with one victory in 10 matches.

Odds correct as of 8.12am on November 10, 2026 from Betfair

#2114. 30-year-old’s goalless run extends to 22 months after short West Ham stay

West Ham saw multiple players depart shortly after their relegation from the Premier League. While valuable assets like Mateus Fernandes and Crysencio Summerville were sold, others left WHUFC at the end of their contracts.

Among those to do so was Adama Traore, who had only arrived from Fulham on a short-term deal in January. He joined to offer depth on the wings for the Hammers, bringing his electric pace and power with him.

However, went goalless in his six months at the London Stadium. This run is part of a whopping 22-month spell without a goal for the 30-year-old winger, who now plays back in his native Spain for Deportivo La Coruna.

Traore has never been a player renowned for his goals, scoring 33 goals in over 450 senior matches across his career. He offers a chaotic presence on the right, with his speed and strength proving too much for plenty of full-backs over the years.

It means he is primarily a creative threat, getting to the byline and delivering for onrushing attackers or box-crashing midfielders. Traore mainly served as an impact sub in his time at West Ham, but he failed to score for the club.

And, back in Spain with Deportivo La Coruna, his wait continues. Traore has mainly played off the bench for the club, and he is yet to score in 10 games across all competitions. It means that, to date, his last goal came in a 2-0 win over Leicester City for Fulham back on January 18th, 2025.

Traore has retained his impact sub role with Deportivo. He completed six successful dribbles and created three chances (FotMob) in 34 minutes off the bench against Osasuna before the international break.

Traore might not be a goalscoring star, but he brings an impact. For better or worse, the physical traits he offers can add an element of unpredictability to attacks, and against tired legs, his speed his a serious threat.

This combined with his strong Championship record means he could have proven to be a handy squad player for West Ham. He previously managed five goals and 10 assists in 35 games in England’s second tier and has added strong pedigree since then.

WHUFC perhaps aren’t longing for Traore given his limited impact after joining in January. However, someone of his unique abilities can make for a real dangerman when chasing a game.

#2112. HMRC chase the estate of late ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson for £3.5MILLION in unpaid tax - because he was 'too busy with his ladies to save'

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 06:19 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 06:25 EST, 10 November 2026

Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased by HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC) for an outstanding £3.5million in tax owed.

It comes as a result of the estate's inheritance following Eriksson's death in August 2024 due to pancreatic cancer.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport last year, the former England manager reportedly had assets worth £4.8m but owed a staggering £7.25m to HMRC alone. He also reportedly had at least £1m outstanding in other debts.

In a bid to help reduce that outstanding debt, his family sold his old mansion called Bjorkefors last year - albeit at a substantial loss.

Eriksson is survived by his son Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39 - from his first marriage to Ann-Christine Pettersson - as well as partner Yaniseth Alcides. During his time as England manager he had a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio.

Speaking to The Sun, Eriksson's lawyer Anders Runebjer has revealed that the estate has no money left to settle the debt - aside from £300,000 in a UK bank and £1m in a Cayman Islands tax haven. He also stated his focus is now to salvage any money for Eriksson's two children after the ex-Three Lions boss had spent his finances around football and women.

Ex-England manager Sven-Goran Eriksson's estate is being chased for £3.5million by HMRC

In August 2024, he passed away at the age of 76 following a battle with pancreatic cancer

The Swede is survived by his two children Johan, 47, and daughter Lina, 39

'Sven earned millions but was always too busy with his football and his ladies to manage money very well,' said Runebjer.

'I told the HMRC I'm not able to get the money in the Cayman Islands or his UK bank and said they're welcome to seize it.

'They replied that they couldn't do that so I told them there was nothing else left - so they won't get paid.

'Sven was regularly sent bills by the British taxman and paid promptly but they changed the rules and now say he still owes £3.5m plus interest after he passed away.

'They're welcome to take whatever they can get but I'm not giving them anything.

'My priority is trying to get whatever money I can that he left for his children - not the British taxman.'

As aforementioned, Eriksson's estate sold his seven-bed house in Torsby, in his native Sweden - located on the banks of Lake Fryken - but at a reduced price.

According to The Sun, the property was on the market for £2m but his family had to lower the price by £400,000 to attract any prospective buyers.

And they went on to add that an anonymous e-commerce businesswoman has now bought it for an undisclosed sum of at least £1.3m - meaning a potential £700,000 loss on market value alone. However, the loss is greater as Eriksson bought the place in 2002 for £4.5m - meaning the true value lost is around £3m.

Last year, Eriksson's former home in Sweden was sold as his family look to reduce debt

Eriksson lived in the property with his partner Yaniseth Alcides until his death

During his time as England boss, he was in a high-profile relationship with Nancy Dell'Olio

Selling the property was the latest thing Eriksson's family have done in a bid to ease the financial burden they have taken on since his death.

In March 2025, they were forced to auction off his memorabilia - such as a lunch invitation from the late Queen.

Also up for auction was his Armani suit from a 2006 World Cup match with his hand-written team notes still in the pocket.

The 349 items reported to have gone under the hammer for a combined total of £140,000 also include his BBC Coach of the Year trophy in 2001 and a Premier League Manager of the Month award from his time as Manchester City boss.

An Ivory Coast top signed with a special message by former forward Didier Drogba from Eriksson's time as national coach in 2010 was sold as well.

Eriksson was estimated to have received around £7m in pay-offs alone from England, Manchester City and Mexico during his managerial career.

The Swede, who managed England between 2001 and 2006, previously described himself as being 'stupid' with his money.

In one of his last ever interviews, he told The Guardian: 'I was never interested in money - I never took care of it and trusted people to do that for me. I was stupid not to control where the money went. I realised that when I didn't have any more cash!

'I still don't know what I have in the bank.'

#2111. 3 players who Wrexham should offload in January, including Ryan Longman

Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson will be keen to add to his ranks, but inconsistent results have been a driving factor behind the Red Dragons’ lowly league position of 15th place.

The North Welsg have several players they could offload in January to free up funds to strengthen the squad, as they aim to close the six-point gap to QPR in the final play-off spot. A hefty outlay in the summer means Wrexham will need to be shrewd in the transfer market, with new arrivals likely requiring some departures to balance the squad.

Here, we take a look at three players Wrexham should look to offload in the winter to freshen up the squad and make way for new arrivals…

The experienced shot-stopper has become a forgotten figure in North Wales with just four appearances to his name since arriving in the summer of 2024.

Burton played second fiddle to Arthur Okonkwo in his debut campaign, before the latter and Danny Ward tussled for the No. 1 shirt last term. The £8m acquisition of Anthony Patterson in the summer has kept Burton as third choice, with his last appearance for the club coming over a year ago in a Carabao Cup defeat to Cardiff City.

Yet to feature in a matchday squad this season, the former Plymouth Argyle man may be enticed by the prospect of regular first-team football.

Ryan Longman has only had one Championship start this season and may seek a new challenge in January.  He asserted himself as a regular at right wing-back, making 21 League One appearances in the second half of the 2024/25 campaign as Wrexham secured promotion.

The 26-year-old was one of their most consistent performers when called upon last season too, deputising on both flanks, with his relentless work rate hailed by the Racecourse Ground faithful.

However, following the permanent acquisition of former loan favourite Issa Kabore from Manchester City in the summer and Danny Imray’s arrival, former Hull City ace Longman has been limited to substitute appearances. He is certainly capable of playing a more prominent role at another club.

Last but not least is Sebastian Revan, who has endured a torrid spell on the sidelines with injury. The defender could benefit from an EFL loan move upon his expected January comeback.

The Aston Villa academy graduate suffered a serious hamstring injury in February during his loan spell at Burton Albion, having made a positive impression under Gary Bowyer after playing a bit-part role in Wrexham’s promotion to the Championship.

His time at the Pirelli Stadium was cut short as he began a long-term rehabilitation programme with his parent club’s medical staff and is nearing a return to action.

Standing in the way of a starting spot is Jacques Ekomie, signed from Angers in the summer and in fine form. It means a loan or permanent exit for Revan looks increasingly likely.

#2110. One league appearance despite trio of assists: How is former Burnley and West Ham target faring since failed summer move

Burnley were a busy side at the end of the transfer window as they looked to strengthen following a disappointing summer and start to the window. The Clarets came close to signing Sunderland winger Jocelin Ta Bi on deadline day in September, but the move ultimately collapsed over the Clarets’ squad requirements.

The 21-year-old had travelled to Turf Moor as Nicky Hayen’s side explored a loan deal, only for the transfer to fall through late in the window. Burnley were not alone in their pursuit, with West Ham, Hull City and several French clubs also expressing interest.

According to reports from Sebastian Denis, the Hammers were among those monitoring Ta Bi throughout the summer, underlining the competition for his signature.

The Ivory Coast youngster joined Sunderland from Maccabi Netanya in January 2026 on a four-and-a-half-year contract. However, regular first-team opportunities have been difficult to come by under Regis Le Bris.

Ta Bi has made limited Premier League appearances, totalling fewer than 60 minutes across his senior outings in England’s top flight. His opportunities have largely come in cup competitions, where he has shown encouraging signs of his potential.

His standout performance came against Brentford in the Carabao Cup on 28 October. Starting on the right wing, Ta Bi was heavily involved in all three Sunderland goals during their 3-2 victory, creating several opportunities and showcasing his ability to beat opponents in wide areas.

Le Bris was particularly impressed by his technical quality, bravery and work rate, highlighting how the youngster managed to combine his attacking contributions with considerable defensive effort.

The Sunderland head coach has previously spoken positively about Ta Bi’s potential, although regular minutes remain important for his development. A temporary move could therefore still make sense, particularly given the player’s limited Premier League involvement.

That is something Burnley should continue monitoring. Ta Bi possesses explosive pace, close control and the dribbling ability to trouble Championship defenders. His preference for cutting inside from the right onto his stronger left foot could also offer a different attacking dimension.

Those qualities would have suited Burnley’s need for greater pace and penetration in the final third under Hayen. Although the Belgian has since departed, the Clarets’ need for more attacking threat has not disappeared.

Ta Bi still has plenty to prove at senior level, but his performance against Brentford demonstrated why Sunderland rate him so highly. If first-team opportunities remain limited, Burnley could have another opportunity to revisit their interest in a player they came so close to signing.

#2109. Bristol City & West Ham ticketing twist has caused a huge backlash

West Ham have enforced a major ticketing decision involving away supporters ahead of next month's home clash against Bristol City - and it's causing quite the reaction online.

Following West Ham's unprecedented relegation from the Premier League back in May, the London Stadium represents the away day for away fans throughout the Championship.

Indeed, the second-tier has never seen a larger ground than the London Stadium's 60,000-capacity, and for virtually every fanbase, an away trip to this corner of East London is one of the most notable fixtures on the calendar all season.

Fans of Bristol City, however, have just received a fresh twist that will impact their fixture away to West Ham next month, with the decision stirring up mixed reaction among supporters online.

Bristol City fans will be ticking off a major Championship away day when they travel to West Ham on December 12, though trips to Middlesbrough, West Bromwich Albion and Derby County are all on the agenda before their journey down the M4 and into East London.

But it has come with a twist that will now see a reduced number of supporters in attendance within the London Stadium away end, with West Ham having reciprocated the Robins' travelling allocation.

A ticketing announcement from the West Country outfit has confirmed this, disclosing that tickets will be on sale to supporters from next Wednesday before revealing the allocation.

Now, the Robins have informed fans that they have received an allocation of just 2,110 tickets including rail seats and general seating. This, of course, is a fairly sizeable reduction on the Hammers' typical away allocation to travelling supporters of around 3,000, yet they've simply reciprocated what City have already done.

Football League World assesses and ranks the FIFTEEN best away fanbases in the EFL right now

The development comes following an announcement in September which revealed that Bristol City have opened the Atyeo Stand to home fans for high-profile fixtures against West Ham, Stoke and Severnside rivals Cardiff, thus reducing the number of tickes available to away supporters.

Therefore, West Ham have reacted by reducing their own allocation for the Robins faithful, and unsurprisingly, it's sparked something of a stir.

With every other Championship club to have travelled to West Ham so far this season having received a larger allocation, fans were quick to react following the Robins' announcement.

A lot of the reaction actually came from Hammers supporters, who wasted no time in lauding their club's reciprocal efforts.

This one fan, for example, applauded his side and urged them to do the same for every game against an opposing club that doesn't provide the same allocation.

Another, meanwhile, kept it direct and straight-to-the-point in response to a Bristol City punter who had questioned the allocation.

Indeed, this West Ham supporter believes the decision is evidence of the East Londoners actually getting something right, with many simply all-too-happy to see that their club has refused to simply roll over and give out the largest possible allocations while being restricted in some of their own travels on the road.

By contrast, Bristol City fans have naturally failed to share the same sentiment and believe that the Robins have been hard done by with this particular decision.

A Robins supporter here pulled no punches by describing it as an "absolute joke" - to which the Hammers' lot were, of course, swift in reminding of why the allocation has been shaved.

Emojis can sometimes tell the story, too, and in this case, they summed up exactly how another supporter of the Ashton Gate side is feeling right now.

However, another punter saw sense behind West Ham's decision and has backed the reciprocation.

There has been a split of opinion over West Ham's allocation for the travelling Bristol City contingent next month, even if many do believe that the Hammers are perfectly within their right to match the reduction.

However, there's absolutely no division when it comes to the prices that West Ham are charging for Robins fans who intend on making the trip to the London Stadium, which may just work out among their cheapest away days all season.

Adult tickets come cheaper than virtually anywhere else in the Championship at just £25, whereas 66+ and under-21 ones are even more affordable at a price of £12.

Under-18 tickets, meanwhile, will cost no more than £10, with these prices across the board paling in comparison to some other second-tier clubs.

West Ham and Bristol City fans, what do you make of this ticketing decision? Is it fair? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below!

All in all, then, Bristol City supporters perhaps can't complain much, and in terms of how much the fixture will cost to attend, there can be no faulting the Hammers.

That's why this fan, despite the noise, took time to praise the prices for City's trip to face Scott Parker's side away from home.

It's also no shock that one West Ham supporter - and many more silently, one can only imagine - hopes that Bristol City undertake some reciprocation of their own by charging the same prices when the promotion-chasers travel to Ashton Gate on New Year's Day.

#2108. Billy Sharp sends EFL Championship promotion warning to Birmingham City

EFL legend and all-time Championship top scorer Billy Sharp has warned Birmingham City that there's still "a long way to go" after Chris Davies' side reached the second-tier summit ahead of the ongoing international break.

The Blues enjoyed an exceptional run of games between the three-week break in September and October and this current one, winning six of their seven games, three by at least a three-goal margin.

They dropped points only at Cardiff City, a side that has yet to lose at home this season, and have maintained their own unbeaten home record, winning all four games to add some gloss to a St Andrew's record which was pretty draw-heavy in the infancy of the campaign.

The win against former table-toppers Swansea City saw them climb above Middlesbrough on goal difference, and they will hold that top spot for at least another week until action resumes ahead of the Christmas period.

The question in the meantime, though, is: Can they stay there?

Billy Sharp has been a regular pundit on EFL shows this season, after formally announcing his retirement from the professional game back in October. The 40-year-old was promoted out of the Championship three times in his career, so he knows what it takes to maintain top-two form.

The all-time Championship top scorer waxed lyrical over Birmingham through the opening 15 games of the campaign, and was actually surprised that their run to the top of the table hasn't been given as much attention as it arguably should have.

FLW looks at which of the division's 24 clubs are the biggest and lowest spenders

"I think you saw glimpses last season, but they obviously didn't have that consistency," he told the Essential EFL Podcast. "They've done it really quietly, actually; no one's really spoken about them.

"He’s got the two settled centre-halves, which I've liked since last season, and I think he's playing a 4-2-3-1, which really suits him at the minute.

"He seems to have a settled side and had a little sprinkle with Millar coming in, adding a bit of magic down the left, and Stansfield got the two goals, which should do him a world of good. We know he’s got the ability, and when he’s firing, he can win games for Birmingham."

It's so far, so good for the Blues this season, but we are just 15 games in. With over two-thirds of the year still to go, and just one point separating Chris Davies' side from West Brom in fifth, Sharp feels that they can't rest on their laurels at all.

"Am I surprised they're top? I am," he admitted. "But we were saying this about Swansea on the last international break.

"It’s still tight at the top, fair play to Birmingham; going into this international break they are top, but there’s still a long way to go."

As Sharp mentioned, Birmingham's current run of six wins in seven to reach the top of the Championship has gone slightly under the radar, with the main second-tier narratives surrounding West Ham United's drop-off, or Middlesbrough struggling without Will Lankshear, for example.

Now, though, this Blues side are at the forefront of the conversation, and will be until league action resumes after the international break. Chris Davies' side are there to be shot at, and all eyes will be on whether they can handle the weight of expectation.

It's arguable that they didn't last season, with many expecting them to follow in the footsteps of Ipswich Town and make it back-to-back promotions after their record-breaking 111-point campaign in League One the year prior.

Pick any two players. Send the code, and your mate enters it here to play the same pair.

But this year, the squad is much more settled. Partnerships which were forming last year are fixed now, and there hasn't been as much squad churn as there was last summer at St Andrew's.

Plus, Chris Davies' decision to move away from a patient, heavy possession-based style has worked wonders, with the Blues packing a real punch in an attacking sense due to their desire to get the ball forward quicker.

They look a lot more ready to maintain results and handle pressure as they become the side teams want to knock off the pedestal.

Sharp also spoke about how this exact conversation was being made around Swansea's chances at promotion, with Vitor Matos' side sitting atop the Championship at the last international break.

And while the Swans did return to action with back-to-back wins, they followed that up with four defeats in five leading up to the break, including that loss at St Andrew's last time out.

They're still in contention, sitting three points off Birmingham, but the difference in performances with the pressure on, compared to when it's not, was there to be seen, and Blues have to guard against the same happening to them.

Do you think Birmingham City can maintain this promotion-winning form? Let us know in the comments.

Chris Davies' side have a tough matchup at Stoke City when play resumes, which then leads them into a run of four games against sides sitting between 18th and 22nd. A win at the bet365 Stadium would propel them into a run of, on paper, easier matches.

Perhaps, by mid-December, this could be a side with some daylight between themselves and the chasing pack, and then people may be taking their current title charge a lot more seriously.

#2107. ‘Embarrassing themselves!’ Jamie Carragher hits back at Rio Ferdinand over Cristiano Ronaldo defence

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Jamie Carragher has taken aim at Rio Ferdinand for defending Cristiano Ronaldo following the Portuguese forward’s latest controversy with his national team.

Ronaldo has found himself at the centre of a growing dispute after abruptly leaving Portugal’s national team camp following a reported disagreement with head coach Jorge Jesus. The incident has prompted strong reactions from former teammates and pundits, with Ferdinand firmly siding with the Al-Nassr star.

Jamie Carragher, however, believes Ronaldo’s reputation should not shield him from criticism when his behaviour becomes difficult to defend.

Rio Ferdinand, who played alongside Cristiano Ronaldo at Manchester United between 2003 and 2009, criticised Jorge Jesus for the way he handled the situation.

Speaking on his Rio Presents podcast, the former United captain criticised Jesus for not showing respect to Cristiano Ronaldo.

“Cristiano Ronaldo was put in a very bad situation and was treated in an inappropriate way. He has an enormous history in football. Jorge Jesus did not deal with Ronaldo well and chose to treat him in that way, but I cannot find any explanation for it,” Ferdinand said.

Despite Jesus being Portugal’s manager, Ferdinand questioned his standing, comparing him with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson and Pep Guardiola. To say the least, Ferdinand only embarrassed himself doing that.

Jamie Carragher saw the argument very differently and rightfully so.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, the former Liverpool defender suggested that Ferdinand’s friendship with Ronaldo was influencing his reaction to the incident.

“People think it’s good to be close to people in the game, but this is where it becomes a problem,” Carragher explained.

He then called out both Ferdinand and broadcaster Piers Morgan, who has also been vocal in his support of Ronaldo.

“People like Piers Morgan and Rio Ferdinand, who are big people in the media whether you like them or not, are embarrassing themselves with the nonsense that they’re coming out with because they know Ronaldo. You can know someone and try to look after them, but you cannot defend the indefensible.”

Carragher believes Ronaldo’s achievements should not put the forward beyond criticism, particularly when his actions involve his national team and its management.

Gary Neville, who also played with Cristiano Ronaldo, has questioned Ronaldo’s handling of the situation, despite his longstanding affection for his former Manchester United teammate.

Neville argued that Ronaldo’s public response had made matters worse and the forward needed to accept criticism rather than expect others to defend him.

“With Cristiano, it’s difficult because I love him, but I can’t watch what happened at United in his second period and then see him make a statement like that without saying something. He has to be pulled up on that and told that it isn’t acceptable,” Neville said.

He also suggested Ronaldo’s extraordinary success, wealth and influence could have contributed to a sense that he was beyond challenge.

“When you have a billion pounds in the bank, the achievements he has had and the power he has, you feel you’re unbreakable, you feel you’re unstoppable,” Neville added.

Despite his criticism, Neville does not believe the episode will define Ronaldo’s legacy permanently. He expects the attention to fade once the forward retires, allowing his achievements on the pitch to take centre stage again.

#2106. Is Mainoo-Tielemans the right midfield option for Man Utd?

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United drew 1-1 at home to Tottenham despite having an extra man advantage. The Reds saw Mbeumo put them in front, but Solanke scored a late leveller in injury time after Bentancur was shown a red card for headbutting Luke Shaw.

Manchester United’s worrisome season continues after accumulating just six points off the first six games, their first start in 40 years. But more than the results, what worries Manchester United is their midfield pairing.

United spent massively on their midfield rebuild and somehow can’t find the best combination in the midfield. Michael Carrick has gone with the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership, but they have failed to control the midfield. Individually, they both come with decent numbers, but collectively they fall short.

Mainoo and Tielemans struggled against Tottenham while closing the midfield and at times showed a lack of energy. On the day when nothing clicked for United, the Mainoo-Tielemans partnership particularly raised eyebrows.

Gary Neville has also raised serious concerns about Manchester United’s Mainoo-Tielemans partnership.

Neville was particularly unimpressed by the midfield balance, arguing that the problems went beyond one disappointing performance.

The former United captain stopped short of ruling out the combination altogether, but he suggested he has serious doubts about its suitability.

“Tielemans and Mainoo, I’m not calling time on it, that’s probably too drastic, but I’ve seen enough of it to think that’s not a midfield that’s dynamic enough to play at this football club in the Premier League.”

Former Spurs midfielder Redknapp felt United struggled to connect their midfield with the rest of the team during the opening stages.

He added: “I didn’t see enough connections in that midfield in the first hour. Baleba came on and did OK and showed a bit more.

“They look devoid of any confidence, any idea, any patterns of play, playing out from the back. Tottenham were much better than them in every single department.”

While Carlos Baleba was a particular highlight on the day, he showed great potential when brought on. He brought a new sense of energy in the midfield and sent a few balls over the top for a couple of quick counterattacks as well.

Redknapp also pointed to the physical demands of modern Premier League football, arguing that United cannot afford to be outworked by their opponents.

Tottenham ran a staggering 5 km more than Manchester United, something Redknapp felt was a pattern.

"Spurs ran 5km more than Man United… it's like that EVERY GAME!"Jamie Redknapp is less than impressed with the lack of ground covered this season by Manchester United 😬 pic.twitter.com/BxWkFuyGJ1

“There is a pattern that I don’t really like when I watch teams, and that’s when every time the stats don’t lie and the other team runs more than you.

“I feel in Premier League football right now there are a couple of non-negotiables, and one is you have to run more than the other team if you want to win or at least get close enough. Tonight Spurs ran 5km more than Manchester United.”

He believes Tottenham’s pressing exposed the lack of pace in United’s midfield, making it difficult for the hosts to move the ball safely through the centre.

“In terms of how they played today, I think they have an issue with Tielemans and Mainoo in midfield. I don’t see enough energy in there. Baleba will add a lot and will give them a tremendous amount of energy but right now, when things aren’t going well… and Tottenham knew it!

“Every time United played the ball out from the back they pounced. They pressed them because they knew United don’t have the pace and speed in midfield to get away.”

“In isolation, one of them is absolutely fine, the two of them together doesn’t work for me. They haven’t got the pace or the energy to get around the pitch for 90 minutes.”

#2105. Bradford City TV decision announced and it's causing a reaction

Bradford City fans have been left extremely frustrated by a television broadcast decision impacting their FA Cup tie against non-league Wimborne Town next month.

The Bantams have endured a dramatic opening to the new League One season, with Michael Duff recently replacing Graham Alexander as the man in the Valley Parade hotseat.

Duff has only overseen one league victory in West Yorkshire so far, but his new employers are certainly going well in cup competitions, yet to lose in the EFL Trophy whilst also making the EFL Cup quarter-finals and reaching the FA Cup second round.

Bradford comfortably dispatched Marine 7-0 on Saturday afternoon, with said victory being rewarded with a high-profile tie against Wimborne, the lowest-ranked side now left in the competition, after the Dorset club defeated League Two side Crawley Town 2-0 on Sunday.

There are, of course, plenty of former Premier League sides competing in the FA Cup's early rounds, and the likelihood of them competing against non-league sides increases the chances of television coverage.

Eight ties were selected for broadcast in the first round proper, and the same number have been chosen again for the second round between December 4th and 7th.

All 24 League One clubs have been ranked in order of size.

Bradford are one of six League One sides who will see their ties televised, with their trip to the Wyatt Homes Stadium kicking off the weekend on Friday, December 4th, with coverage beginning on TNT Sports 1 at 7PM ahead of a 7:30PM kick-off.

Other televised ties include 2021 FA Cup winners, Leicester City's trip to Dover Athletic, which now kicks off at 5:15PM on Saturday, December 5th on BBC Two.

It is approximately five hours' worth of travel from the West Yorkshire city to the town of Wimborne Minster, meaning that, at the best of times, an arduous journey would be in store for the Bradford fans.

Crawley supporters received an allocation of 500 tickets in the 3,250-capacity ground last weekend, and a similar number will be expected to make the trip to support Duff's men.

However, whilst City fans are likely to sell out such a figure, the decision to now play the game on a Friday night just three weeks before Christmas hasn't gone down well at all, with one supporter saying: "Asking people to take a day off work to go do a 10 hour round trip to Winbourne is crazy. Deserves boosted loyalty points imo."

Another said of the decision: "Friday night on the south coast. Seeing as there will only be about 200 tickets it should reduce demand."

"Did we really expect anything else - well actually the way the schedulers don't give a damn about travel times I had a feeling it might have been Monday!," one displeased City fan wrote.

"Who makes these decisions," questioned another Bantams supporter.

Bradford fans, will you be making the long journey to Wimborne for this FA Cup tie? Comment below!

Another verdict read: "Teed up perfectly for #bcafc to be on the receiving end of an FA Cup shock. Friday night, tight ground, locals right up for it, live tv....all the ingredients right there!"

"Honestly mind boggling who makes these decisions. Fair play to anyone who makes that journey on a Friday night," backed up the general feeling amongst Bradford's fanbase.

Wimborne are currently ninth in the Southern Football League Premier Division South, with four steps in the English pyramid separating themselves from Bradford.

As such, the wider public will certainly be hoping the non-league side reach the third round and potentially pluck out a 'glamour tie' involving a Premier League or high-flying Championship outfit.

Five players, five careers. Name them from the clubs they played for.

Each day there are five current or former EFL players to identify. For each one you’ll see their senior clubs in the order they played for them. Loan spells are left out.

You get four guesses per player. Every wrong guess unlocks a clue: first their position, then their nationality, then their initials.

Get it first time for 4 points, then 3, 2 and 1. The best possible score is 20. A new set of players arrives at midnight.

#2104. One lesson Senne Lammens learned after Tottenham’s late equaliser

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Senne Lammens believes Manchester United must learn to finish games off after their late collapse against Tottenham Hotspur.

The result left the goalkeeper frustrated at Old Trafford despite leading the game and with a player more on the field.

Manchester United looked set for three points after Bryan Mbeumo put them ahead in the second half, but Dominic Solanke’s stoppage-time equaliser denied Michael Carrick’s side a much-needed victory.

Speaking to MUTV, Senne Lammens admitted the team had struggled early on but had done enough after the break to put themselves in a winning position.

“Football can be a bit cruel at times,” the Belgian goalkeeper said. “There are a lot of ups and downs, especially in a game like that.”

Senne Lammens felt United failed to take advantage of Tottenham’s red card, allowing the visitors too much space to find a late equaliser.

“We’ve won a lot of games against 10 men [in the past], but you also know there can be a tricky situation when you’re playing against 10 men, because they have nothing to lose and they know that.”

He added that United should have scored again to put the result beyond doubt or, at the very least, prevented Tottenham from creating further chances.

“I think that’s what we did wrong. We gave them a little bit too much breathing room to create those chances, and then one ball has to go right for them, one bounce has to go their way, and they can score like that.”

The goalkeeper also pointed to similarities with United’s earlier disappointment against Everton, where points slipped away late in the match.

“You feel like those games just slip away from you, and there are one or two situations where you don’t really have control,” he said.

“I think there’s a lot to learn from today. It wasn’t all negative, not at all, but especially the way it ended left a very bad feeling.”

“I think the easy answer is that we have to be able to kill the game faster and not put ourselves in that position to give them a chance.”

Despite the frustration, Lammens said there were positives to take from the performance. However, the late goal had left a bitter feeling, and United now need to turn those lessons into better results.

#2103. Manchester United defence: Why Carrick must trust Yoro and Heaven

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United endured another embarrassing draw against 10-man Tottenham after failing to register their second win despite bringing in a plethora of players.

Manchester United invested heavily last season in their attacking options, bringing in Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha.

This season, they overhauled their midfield. United spent massively on Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. Despite spending massively, they have failed to produce the control they would have expected in the midfield. The lack of control was evident in the recent Tottenham game, where Mainoo-Tielemans partnership failed to control the game collectively.

The midfield question was covered in our recent report as well, highlighting a lack of control and carried comments from Gary Neville and Jamie Redknapp.

The bigger question is when United will strengthen their defence. As per our previous report as well, Manchester United are planning to overhaul their defence in the upcoming transfer windows.

United were heavily linked with several left backs but eventually failed to bring any one. The situation left Luke Shaw as the only senior option in the position, while Patrick Dorgu is used upfront by Michael Carrick.

Harry Amass is another option for Michael Carrick, but he is only here because of a failed transfer move. He has been rarely used at left back as Dalot and Mazraoui get the nod in the position ahead of him.

The situation at right-back isn’t all good either. Diogo Dalot is the first option there, but he rarely provides the assurance that puts Michael Carrick at ease. Noussair Mazraoui is the second choice at right-back, but his attacking numbers aren’t great either.

Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez form up United’s centre-back pairing while Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven are used all over the defensive line in rotation when needed. Yoro was used at right-back against Tottenham while Heaven arrived as left-back towards the end of the game.

Manchester United’s season hasn’t been defensively strong or anywhere near being good. They have conceded goals in all Premier League games and only kept one clean sheet against Sabah in the Champions League.

Lisandro Martinez has come under scrutiny after errors on four occasions. Against Ipswich Town, Manchester United won 5-2, but his error resulted in Ipswich’s second goal.

His own goal against Fulham gave away two points at Craven Cottage in the 1-1 draw. Another error led to Solanke’s goal against Tottenham, when he took his eyes off the ball.

His injury concerns are another aspect, and maybe Michael Carrick needs to make a decision.

Manchester United’s success depended heavily on youth over the years. When pundits questioned them, Sir Alex Ferguson gave them the chance to prove them wrong. Alan Hansen made the famous quote “You can’t win anything with kids” on the BBC’s Match of the Day on August 19, 1995. United did exactly that, played youth and went on to win everything.

Michael Carrick needs to do exactly that. He needs to trust youth and allow them to make mistakes. Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven arrived as massive potentials, but they haven’t been given the license to express themselves, without fearing for their places. Both the youngsters have rarely started together or in a stretch of games. It is maybe time for them to take their chances.

Michael Carrick needs to keep Harry Maguire as a senior experienced figure around them. There is no doubt over Martinez’s ability, but he is not the answer to United’s long-term problem. United need to blend youth with experience as their identity moving forward. Lisandro Martinez perhaps isn’t the answer to United’s problem.

A defensive revival expected in the upcoming transfer windows needs to happen now. It must happen with chances to the Youth. Michael Carrick needs to be brave enough and throw the youngsters in the mix. What it will bring is a long-term solution. They need to experience the errors and pressures that will shape them in football.

#2102. Notts County confirm TV decision and it's sparked backlash

Notts County's League One struggles look to be over after their four matches in a row lost in September and October, with Martin Paterson finally finding the winning formula again.

Paterson guided the Magpies back into League One earlier this year with a resounding League Two play-off final victory over Salford City, and he was backed by the Reedtz Brothers with some exciting cash signings and eye-catching loanees.

Football League World runs down their Team of the Season in League One so far this term

County were in the relegation zone of the third tier in mid-October after four defeats on the spin, but wins over Sheffield Wednesday and Mansfield Town, as well as a respectable draw at home to Stockport County, has seen the mood lift at Meadow Lane, and the pressure somewhat rise from Paterson's shoulders.

Last weekend, Notts County stepped away from league action to take part in Round One of the FA Cup, where they were handed a potential banana skin in the form of National League side Altrincham.

In-front of over 4,000 fans at Moss Lane, County went 2-1 behind to the fifth tier outfit, only for Cal Roberts to rescue the game in the 84th-minute and send it to extra time.

And despite the deteriorating foggy conditions, Notts County won out in the resulting penalty shootout, despite the lack of visibility for their supporters at the opposite end of the ground.

One of 40 clubs that were in Monday's second round draw, Notts were handed a tie against a club even further down the footballing pyramid than their previous opponents, with a trip to Northern Premier League side Guiseley on the horizon.
